_comment: Curated recipe database for khaana.com. Version-controlled: edit here and the Cook page and recipe pages update. Ingredient ids must exist in data/pantry.json. Photography is Wikimedia Commons, credited per recipe and in CREDITS.md.

recipes.name: Aloo ki Tehri
recipes.subtitle: the one-pot turmeric rice and potato dinner every Lucknow household falls back on

ingredients.note: mustard oil works and is more everyday

prepNotes: Soak the rice 30 minutes and drain it well in a sieve for 10 minutes — wet rice clumps in the pan.
Measure the water exactly. Tehri is cooked by absorption, so 1 part rice to 2 parts water by volume, no guessing.
Cut the potatoes just before cooking and keep them in water so they do not brown.

steps.text: Heat the ghee in a heavy pot and crackle the cumin, bay leaf, cloves, cardamom and cinnamon for 30 seconds.
Add the onion and fry 8 minutes over medium heat, until evenly golden brown.
Add the ginger and green chillies, fry 1 minute, then the potato chunks. Fry 5 minutes until their edges pick up colour.
steps.tip: Browning the potato now keeps the pieces intact later instead of crumbling into the rice.

steps.text: Stir in the turmeric, coriander powder and salt with 2 tbsp water and cook 1 minute.
Add the drained rice and peas and turn everything over gently for 2 minutes, until every grain is coated and glossy.
steps.tip: Use a flat spatula and fold — stirring hard breaks the soaked grains.

steps.text: Pour in the hot water, bring to a rolling boil, then taste for salt and let it boil uncovered 4 minutes until the water level drops to the rice.
Cover tightly, drop the heat to the lowest setting and cook 12 minutes without lifting the lid.
Take off the heat, sprinkle over the garam masala, and rest covered 10 minutes before opening.
steps.tip: The rest is not optional — the grains finish steaming and firm up in these ten minutes.

steps.text: Fluff with a fork, fold in the coriander leaves and serve with plain yogurt and a raw onion salad.

recipes.storage: Keeps 2 days refrigerated. Reheat by sprinkling over 2 tbsp water and steaming covered on low for 6 minutes; microwaving dries the grains.

recipes.name: Arhar ki Dal
recipes.subtitle: the plain everyday toor dal of Lucknow homes, finished with a loud ghee, cumin and hing tadka

ingredients.qty: 1 cup (200g), rinsed until the water runs clear

ingredients.note: the whole point of the tadka
use compounded-free hing if you need this gluten-free

prepNotes: Soak the dal 20 minutes while you chop — it shaves ten minutes off the cooking and gives a creamier finish.
Have the tadka ingredients measured out beside the stove. From cumin to chilli the whole thing takes under a minute and burns easily.

steps.text: Put the dal, water, turmeric, tomato and half the salt in a pressure cooker. Cook on high for 4 whistles, then let the pressure drop by itself, about 10 minutes.
Open up and whisk the dal briskly for 20 seconds. It should be loose and pourable, like thin cream — add hot water if it has tightened.
steps.tip: Whisking, not stirring, is what makes home dal smooth.

steps.text: Add the slit green chillies and simmer uncovered 5 minutes so the dal takes on their scent.
Heat the ghee in a small pan until it shimmers. Add the cumin and let it crackle and darken by a shade, about 15 seconds.
Drop in the hing, then the broken red chillies, then the sliced garlic and ginger. Fry 30-40 seconds, until the garlic is pale gold.
steps.tip: Hing goes in first and briefly — it scorches faster than anything else in the pan.

steps.text: Pour the tadka straight into the dal and clap the lid on for 2 minutes to trap the aroma.
Stir in the lemon juice and the rest of the salt off the heat, taste, and scatter the coriander leaves.
steps.tip: Lemon after the heat is off — boiled lemon juice turns bitter.

recipes.storage: Keeps 3 days refrigerated and thickens as it sits. Loosen with hot water when reheating; a fresh half-tadka of ghee and cumin brings it back to life.

recipes.name: Awadhi Kheer
recipes.subtitle: slow-reduced rice pudding scented with saffron, cardamom and a drop of kewra

ingredients.note: broken coarsely between the palms for a thicker set
for rubbing the pan so the milk does not catch

ingredients.qty: a generous pinch, steeped in 2 tbsp warm milk

ingredients.note: a few drops; it dominates quickly

prepNotes: Soak the rice 20 minutes, drain, then crush it lightly between your palms so the grains break in two. Broken rice gives a creamier kheer.
Steep the saffron in warm milk for 20 minutes before you begin.
Rub the base of a heavy pan with ghee before adding the milk — it makes the difference between kheer and scorched milk.

steps.text: Rub the pan with ghee, pour in the milk and bring it to a boil over medium heat, stirring.
Add the drained, crushed rice and lower the heat so the milk simmers gently.
Cook uncovered 45–50 minutes, stirring and scraping the base every 4–5 minutes, until the rice is soft and the milk has reduced by nearly half.
steps.tip: Scrape the bottom each time, not just the top. That is where it catches and turns bitter.

steps.text: Push the cream that forms on the sides back into the pan as you go.
Add the sugar and stir 8 minutes until it dissolves and the kheer thickens again.
steps.tip: Sugar goes in only once the rice is fully soft; added early it stops the grains softening.

steps.text: Stir in the saffron milk and cook 4 minutes until the colour is even.
Add the cardamom powder, almonds, pistachios and raisins and cook 2 minutes.
Take off the heat, stir in the kewra water, and let it stand 15 minutes.
steps.tip: It thickens noticeably as it cools — pull it off the heat looser than you want it.

steps.text: Serve warm, or chill 2 hours and serve cold with extra slivered pistachios.

recipes.storage: Keeps 3 days refrigerated in a covered container. It sets firm when cold; loosen with 2–3 tbsp warm milk and stir before serving. Do not freeze.

recipes.name: Awadhi Murgh Masala
recipes.subtitle: everyday bone-in chicken curry, browned onion and yogurt with ground cashew, gentle on chilli

ingredients.note: half ghee and half neutral oil is common at home
a modern addition; leave it out for the older version

prepNotes: Marinate the chicken in the yogurt with salt and turmeric for 30 minutes at room temperature.
Soak the cashews in hot water for 20 minutes so they blend without grit.
Slice the onions as thin as you can manage — thick slices never brown evenly.

steps.text: Heat the ghee, add the bay leaf, cardamom, cloves and cinnamon and let them swell for 30 seconds.
Add the sliced onion and cook over medium heat, stirring, until deep golden brown, 12–14 minutes.
steps.tip: This is where the colour and sweetness of the curry comes from. Do not shorten it.

steps.text: Stir in the ginger and garlic pastes and fry 2 minutes until the raw smell goes.
Add the coriander powder, cumin powder, kashmiri chilli and 2 tbsp water and bhuno 2 minutes.
steps.tip: The splash of water keeps the ground spices from scorching.

steps.text: Add the chopped tomato, if using, and cook until it breaks down completely, 4 minutes.
Lower the flame, add the marinated chicken with all its yogurt and stir constantly for 8 minutes until the fat separates and the pieces are coated.
steps.tip: Keep it on low and keep stirring or the yogurt will split.

steps.text: Blend the soaked cashews with 4 tbsp water to a smooth paste and stir it in with the salt.
Pour in 300ml warm water, cover and simmer 18–20 minutes until the chicken is tender and the gravy has thickened.
Uncover, add the garam masala and crushed kasuri methi and reduce 3 minutes.
Rest covered 5 minutes, scatter with coriander leaves and serve with paratha or rice.

recipes.storage: Keeps 3 days refrigerated and freezes well for a month. Reheat covered on low with a splash of water.

recipes.name: Awadhi Paneer Korma
recipes.subtitle: paneer in an ivory cashew and yogurt gravy, mild and heavily perfumed

ingredients.qty: a pinch in 2 tbsp warm milk

ingredients.note: a few drops only; it takes over quickly

prepNotes: Soak the paneer cubes in warm salted water for 15 minutes while you build the gravy. They stay soft instead of turning rubbery.
Bring the yogurt to room temperature and whisk it completely smooth before it goes anywhere near the pan.
Grind the cashew paste first and keep it beside the stove — it goes in at a moment when you cannot leave the pan.

steps.text: Fry the sliced onion in 2 tbsp ghee over medium heat until pale gold and soft, 8 minutes. Do not let it brown.
steps.tip: Brown onion makes a fine korma, just not a white one. Pale gold is the target.

steps.text: Cool the onion and grind it with the soaked cashews, melon seeds and 4 tbsp water to a completely smooth paste.
Heat the remaining 2 tbsp ghee, add the ginger and garlic pastes and fry 90 seconds until the raw edge is gone.
Add the onion-cashew paste and cook on low for 6 minutes, stirring often, until it thickens and no longer smells raw.
steps.tip: It catches easily. Keep the spoon moving and the flame low.

steps.text: Take the pan off the heat and whisk in the yogurt in three additions, then return to the lowest flame for 5 minutes until the ghee shows at the edges.
Stir in the coriander powder, fennel powder, mace, white pepper, green chillies and salt and cook 2 minutes.
Add 250ml warm water and simmer uncovered 6 minutes until the gravy coats a spoon.
Drain the paneer, slip it in and simmer 4 minutes only.
steps.tip: Longer than this and the paneer tightens up. It only needs to warm through.

steps.text: Finish with cream, cardamom powder, saffron milk and a few drops of kewra water. Rest covered 5 minutes before serving.

recipes.storage: Keeps 2 days refrigerated. Reheat on low with a splash of milk; the paneer firms up in the fridge and softens again as it warms. Do not freeze.

recipes.name: Bhindi do Pyaza
recipes.subtitle: dry-fried okra with twice its weight in onion, sharp with amchur and mustard oil

ingredients.qty: 500g, wiped dry and cut into 3cm lengths
3 medium — 2 quartered and separated into petals, 1 finely sliced
ingredients.note: the two cuts are what 'do pyaza' means here
or neutral oil, but mustard oil is the Lucknow default
added at the end

prepNotes: Wash the okra an hour ahead and dry each pod with a cloth. Any water left on them and the dish turns slimy.
Cut the okra only once the pan is hot — cut okra sitting around weeps.
If using mustard oil, heat it to smoking first and cool it slightly before cooking to take off the raw pungency.

steps.text: Heat the mustard oil in a kadhai until it smokes faintly, then lower the heat and let it settle for 30 seconds.
Add the cumin seeds and let them crackle, 15 seconds, then tip in the okra with 1/2 tsp salt.
Fry the okra on medium-high heat, stirring only every couple of minutes, for 8-10 minutes, until the edges brown and the pods stop looking sticky.
steps.tip: Stirring constantly is what makes bhindi slimy. Leave it alone and let it sear.

steps.text: Lift the okra out onto a plate. Add the sliced onion to the same pan and cook 4 minutes until it softens and turns gold at the edges.
Add the onion petals and green chillies and fry 3 minutes on high — they should stay crunchy and separate, not collapse.
Lower the heat, add the turmeric, coriander, chilli and fennel powders with a splash of water and fry 1 minute to bloom the spices.
Return the okra, add the remaining salt and toss gently for 3 minutes until everything is coated.
Sprinkle over the amchur and garam masala, toss once and take off the heat immediately.
steps.tip: Amchur goes in off the flame; cooked long it goes flat and slightly bitter.

recipes.storage: Best eaten the day it is made — refrigerated it keeps 2 days but softens. Reheat in a dry pan on high heat, never covered, or the okra steams and goes limp.

recipes.name: Boti Kebab
recipes.subtitle: yogurt-marinated mutton cubes, charred outside and juicy through

ingredients.note: thin yogurt slides off the meat
tenderiser; skip only if using very young goat
colour without much heat

ingredients.qty: 2 tbsp, heated to smoking and cooled

ingredients.note: stops the yogurt from weeping in the heat

prepNotes: Marinate at least 4 hours, ideally overnight, refrigerated. Under 2 hours and the mutton stays tough.
Take the meat out of the fridge 30 minutes before cooking so it grills evenly.
Roast the besan in a dry pan until it smells nutty and cool it before it goes near the yogurt.

steps.text: Pat the mutton cubes completely dry and prick each one two or three times with a fork.
Rub in the papaya paste, ginger, garlic and salt and leave 20 minutes.
Whisk the hung yogurt with the roasted besan, kashmiri chilli, coriander powder, garam masala, black pepper and the cooled mustard oil until smooth.
steps.tip: Smoked-then-cooled mustard oil loses its raw bite but keeps the pungency.

steps.text: Fold the meat through the marinade, cover and refrigerate overnight.
Thread onto skewers with a finger gap between cubes so the heat gets all the way round.
steps.tip: Packed tight, they steam instead of charring.

steps.text: Grill over medium-hot charcoal or under an oven grill at 240C for 12–15 minutes, turning every 3 minutes.
Baste with ghee in the last 4 minutes and let the edges blacken in patches.
Rest 3 minutes off the heat, then dust with chaat masala and squeeze over lemon.
steps.tip: Resting lets the juices settle; cut one straight away and it bleeds out.

recipes.storage: Eat within the hour. Marinated raw meat keeps 2 days refrigerated. Leftover cooked boti is best chopped into a paratha roll rather than reheated whole.

recipes.name: Dahi ke Kebab
recipes.subtitle: crisp-shelled hung yogurt kebabs that dissolve into cream the moment you bite

ingredients.qty: 800g full-fat, hung overnight to give about 350g thick curd

ingredients.note: adds body so they hold shape

ingredients.qty: 3 tbsp, dry-roasted until it smells nutty
4 slices, crusts off, blitzed to crumbs
ingredients.note: for coating

prepNotes: Hang the yogurt in muslin overnight in the fridge with a weight on top. It must be dry enough to crumble, not spoonable — this is the whole recipe.
Roast the besan in a dry pan until it turns a shade darker and smells like toasted flour, then cool it completely before mixing.
Chill the shaped kebabs 20 minutes before frying so they set.

steps.text: Tip the hung yogurt into a bowl and mash in the grated paneer until smooth and even.
Squeeze the chopped onion in your fist over the sink to wring out its water, then fold it in with the green chilli, ginger, cardamom, white pepper, coriander leaves and salt.
steps.tip: Wet onion is the usual reason these kebabs fall apart in the pan.

steps.text: Work in the roasted besan a tablespoon at a time until the mixture just holds a shape when pressed. It should feel soft, almost too soft.
Rest the mix 15 minutes, then shape into 10 flat discs about 5cm across and 1.5cm thick with lightly oiled palms.
Press each disc into the breadcrumbs on both sides and on the rim, then chill 20 minutes on a lined tray.
Heat 2 tbsp ghee on a tawa over medium-low heat. Lay in half the kebabs, leaving space between them.
steps.tip: Medium-low. High heat browns the crumb before the inside warms and the kebab bursts.

steps.text: Fry undisturbed 3-4 minutes, until the underside is set and deep gold, then turn once with a thin spatula and give the second side 3 minutes.
steps.tip: Turn once only. Every flip after that is a chance for them to break.

steps.text: Drain briefly on paper, repeat with the rest, dust with chaat masala and serve hot with mint chutney.

recipes.storage: Eat them straight from the pan; they soften within the hour. The uncooked shaped kebabs keep 24 hours refrigerated on a covered tray and actually fry better cold.

recipes.name: Dum Aloo Lucknowi
recipes.subtitle: fried baby potatoes finished in a yogurt gravy with fennel and dry ginger, no onion or garlic

ingredients.qty: 500g baby potatoes, boiled 10 minutes and peeled

ingredients.note: use compounded-free hing to keep the dish gluten-free
the defining flavour here
saunth stands in for fresh ginger in a no-onion-garlic kitchen

prepNotes: Boil the potatoes only until a skewer goes in with slight resistance, then cool and peel. Fully soft potatoes collapse in the fryer.
Prick each peeled potato all over with a fork or toothpick — that is how the gravy gets inside.
Whisk the yogurt with the dry spices before it goes in the pan; the powders stop it splitting.

steps.text: Prick the boiled, peeled potatoes deeply all over and pat them dry.
Deep fry them in hot oil until golden and lightly blistered, 4–5 minutes. Drain and set aside.
steps.tip: Dry potatoes only — wet ones spit violently in hot oil.

steps.text: Whisk the yogurt with the coriander powder, kashmiri chilli, turmeric, fennel powder and dry ginger powder to a smooth, lump-free mix.
Heat the ghee in a kadhai, add the bay leaf, cardamom, cloves, cinnamon and cumin seeds and let them crackle 30 seconds.
Add the asafoetida, count to five, then immediately pour in the spiced yogurt.
steps.tip: Hing burns in seconds. It goes in last and the yogurt follows straight after.

steps.text: Cook on the lowest flame, stirring without stopping, for 7–8 minutes until the mixture thickens and the ghee separates.
steps.tip: Stop stirring and it curdles. This is the one step that needs your full attention.

steps.text: Add the fried potatoes and salt and turn them through the masala for 3 minutes.
Pour in 250ml warm water, bring to a simmer, then cover tightly and cook on the lowest heat for 15 minutes.
Uncover, stir in the garam masala and crushed kasuri methi and reduce 3 minutes until the gravy clings to the potatoes.
Rest covered 5 minutes before serving with sheermal or plain rice.

recipes.storage: Keeps 3 days refrigerated and the potatoes absorb more flavour overnight. Reheat covered on low with a splash of water. Do not freeze — the potatoes turn grainy.

recipes.name: Galouti Kebab
recipes.subtitle: Minced mutton kebabs so soft they collapse on the tongue, from the Nawab's kitchen

ingredients.note: the tenderiser that gives galouti its name
only if the mix will not hold

prepNotes: Galouti was reputedly made for a Nawab who had lost his teeth, so texture is the whole point: the mince must be ground to a paste, not merely chopped.
Raw papaya paste is the tenderiser. Do not overdo it or the meat turns mushy, and do not marinate longer than an hour.

steps.text: Blend the mince to a smooth paste with the papaya, ginger and garlic. Rest 45 minutes, refrigerated.
Fry the sliced onion in ghee until deep brown, drain, cool and crush to a powder. This birista carries most of the sweetness.
steps.tip: Browned, not burnt — bitter birista ruins the kebab.

steps.text: Work the birista, ground cashew, garam masala, mace, nutmeg, cardamom, saffron milk and salt into the mince. It should be soft but hold a shape; add the roasted besan only if it will not.
Chill the mix 30 minutes, then shape into flat discs about 6cm across and 1cm thick.
Fry on a tawa in ghee over low-medium heat, 3-4 minutes a side. Turn once and gently — they are fragile.
steps.tip: Low heat: high heat sets a crust before the centre cooks.

steps.text: Serve immediately with ulte tawe ka paratha or plain sheermal.

recipes.storage: Best straight from the pan. The raw mix keeps 24 hours refrigerated and shapes better cold; cooked kebabs reheat poorly and dry out.

recipes.name: Kakori Kebab
recipes.subtitle: silky skewered mutton mince, perfumed with mace and khoya, that barely holds its shape

ingredients.qty: 500g leg mince, put through the mincer twice
ingredients.note: ask for the fine plate
the tenderiser — do not increase it

ingredients.qty: 2 medium, thinly sliced and fried to brown birista

ingredients.note: gives the fat that keeps the mince soft
the signature note of a kakori

ingredients.qty: a generous pinch, soaked in 1 tbsp warm milk

prepNotes: Marinate the mince 2 hours refrigerated, no longer. Papaya keeps working and past that the meat goes pasty.
Soak wooden skewers 30 minutes, or use flat metal ones — round skewers let the mince spin off.
Chill the mince hard before shaping. Cold mince grips the skewer; warm mince slides.

steps.text: Fry the sliced onion in 3 tbsp ghee over medium heat until evenly deep brown, 10–12 minutes. Drain, cool until crisp, then crush to a powder.
steps.tip: Pull it out at brown, not black — burnt birista turns the whole kebab bitter.

steps.text: Blend the mince with the papaya paste, ginger and garlic to a smooth, almost creamy paste.
Work in the birista powder, ground cashew, almond, poppy seed, khoya, mace, nutmeg, cardamom, white pepper, garam masala, saffron milk, kewra and salt.
Cover and refrigerate 2 hours, then chill in the freezer 15 minutes just before shaping.
Wet your palm and press the mince along a flat skewer in a sausage about 15cm long and 2cm thick, tapering the ends.
steps.tip: Wet hands, light pressure. Squeezing warms the fat and the kebab cracks.

steps.text: Grill over medium charcoal or in an oven at 220C, turning every 3 minutes and basting with ghee, for 12–15 minutes total.
Finish 1 minute directly over high heat to colour the outside.
steps.tip: Watch it — with this much fat it goes from browned to charred in seconds.

steps.text: Slide off the skewer, rest 2 minutes, and serve with sheermal and onion rings.

recipes.storage: Best eaten straight off the skewer. The raw marinated mince keeps 24 hours refrigerated; cooked kebabs dry out badly on reheating, so cook only what you will eat.

recipes.name: Kali Mirch ka Murgh
recipes.subtitle: pale peppery chicken in a white onion-and-cashew gravy with no chilli at all

ingredients.note: crush it fresh, the whole dish rests on this

ingredients.qty: 2 medium, boiled 10 minutes and ground to a smooth paste
ingredients.note: boiling keeps the gravy pale

ingredients.qty: 15, soaked in hot water and ground

prepNotes: Marinate the chicken in the yogurt, ginger, garlic, half the black pepper and 1 tsp salt for at least 1 hour, refrigerated.
Boil and grind the onion while the chicken marinates; the paste should be silky with no fibres left.
Bring the marinated chicken to room temperature 20 minutes before cooking.

steps.text: Heat the ghee on medium and drop in the bay leaf, cloves and cardamom. Give them 30 seconds, until they puff and perfume the fat.
Add the boiled onion paste and cook 6-7 minutes, stirring often, until it loses its raw smell but stays ivory.
steps.tip: Keep the heat medium-low. Any browning here and it is no longer a white gravy.

steps.text: Stir in the cashew paste and cook 3 minutes more, until the mixture thickens and pulls away from the base.
Add the marinated chicken with all its yogurt and fry on medium heat for 6 minutes, until the pieces turn opaque and firm.
Add the salt, pour in the hot water, cover and simmer 18-20 minutes, until the chicken is tender and the gravy coats a spoon.
Uncover and stir in the remaining black pepper and the white pepper. Simmer 3 minutes so the heat blooms in the gravy.
steps.tip: Late pepper stays fragrant and sharp; pepper added early goes flat and dusty.

steps.text: Swirl in the cream, take off the heat and rest 5 minutes covered.
Scatter the coriander leaves and serve with roomali roti or plain steamed rice.

recipes.storage: Keeps 2 days refrigerated. Reheat on low with a splash of milk or water — hard boiling will split the yogurt and cream.

recipes.name: Kathal ki Sabzi
recipes.subtitle: raw jackfruit browned in mustard oil and simmered in a dark bhuna masala, meaty enough to fool anyone

ingredients.note: oil your hands and the knife first, the sap is glue
4 for frying the jackfruit, 2 for the masala

prepNotes: Rub oil on your palms and knife before you touch the jackfruit — the latex sap will not wash off otherwise.
Toss the cut pieces with 1/2 tsp salt and 1/4 tsp turmeric and leave 15 minutes; they fry to a better colour.
Heat the mustard oil to smoking once at the start and let it cool a little — raw mustard oil is harsh.

steps.text: Heat 4 tbsp mustard oil in a kadhai and fry the jackfruit in two batches over medium heat, 6-7 minutes a batch, turning until the pieces are gold on all faces. Drain and set aside.
steps.tip: Crowding the pan steams the jackfruit and it will never brown. Two batches, no shortcuts.

steps.text: Add the remaining 2 tbsp oil, then the cumin, bay leaf and black cardamom. Let them crackle 30 seconds.
Add the sliced onion and fry 10-12 minutes over medium heat until deep brown at the edges.
Stir in the ginger and garlic pastes and cook 2 minutes, until the sharp smell lifts.
Add the turmeric, coriander, chilli and fennel powders with 2 tbsp water and fry 1 minute.
Pour in the tomato puree and salt. Bhuno on medium heat 8-10 minutes, until the masala darkens and oil beads out at the sides.
steps.tip: This is the step that decides the dish. Stop only when you can see clear oil separating.

steps.text: Return the jackfruit, turn it through the masala for 2 minutes, then add the hot water.
Cover and simmer on low 15-18 minutes, until a knife slides into a piece with no resistance and the gravy clings.
Sprinkle the garam masala, cover off the heat for 5 minutes, then finish with the coriander leaves.

recipes.storage: Keeps 3 days refrigerated and improves overnight as the jackfruit absorbs the masala. Reheat covered on low with 2 tbsp water.

recipes.name: Lucknowi Dum Biryani
recipes.subtitle: Pakki biryani: meat and rice cooked separately, then sealed and finished on dum

ingredients.qty: a good pinch in 1/4 cup warm milk

ingredients.note: only seals the lid and is discarded, so the dish stays gluten-free

prepNotes: Awadhi biryani is subtle by design — where Hyderabadi is fiery, this is perfumed. Resist adding chilli powder or turmeric; the colour should be white and gold, not red.
Rice is boiled to 70% before layering. Fully cooked rice turns to paste on dum.

steps.text: Cook the mutton with yogurt, ginger, garlic, half the birista, the whole spices and salt until tender and almost dry, about 45 minutes. This is the korma base.
Boil the soaked rice in heavily salted water with a bay leaf until it is 70% done — the grain should still have a firm core when pressed.
steps.tip: Drain the moment it reaches that stage; it keeps cooking on dum.

steps.text: Layer: meat at the bottom, rice over it, then the saffron milk, remaining birista, mint, kewra and ghee across the top.
Seal the lid with a rope of atta dough, or cover tightly with foil and a lid.
Cook on the lowest possible heat for 25 minutes — over a tawa if your burner runs hot — or in a 160C oven.
Rest 10 minutes before breaking the seal, then lift from the bottom with a flat spoon so the grains stay whole.

recipes.storage: Keeps 2 days refrigerated. Reheat covered with a sprinkle of water so the rice steams rather than fries. Freezing makes the grains brittle.

recipes.name: Murgh Korma
recipes.subtitle: pale, fragrant chicken in a yogurt and cashew gravy with no chilli heat to speak of

ingredients.note: bone-in gives the gravy its body
two for birista, one for the paste
the quiet sweetness behind an Awadhi gravy
heat without staining the gravy

ingredients.qty: a pinch in 2 tbsp warm milk

prepNotes: Bring the yogurt to room temperature and whisk it loose. Cold yogurt straight from the fridge splits on contact.
Soak the cashews in hot water 20 minutes so the paste grinds silky rather than grainy.
This is a white gravy: no tomato, no browning of the chicken. Keep the heat low throughout.

steps.text: Fry two sliced onions in 3 tbsp ghee over medium heat until evenly brown, 10–12 minutes. Drain and reserve the birista.
Grind the soaked cashews, almonds and half the birista to a smooth paste with 4 tbsp water.
In the same ghee add the remaining ghee, bay leaf, cardamom, cloves and cinnamon and let them swell for 30 seconds.
Add the third sliced onion and cook gently until soft and pale gold, 6 minutes, without letting it colour further.
steps.tip: Any darkening here and the finished korma goes muddy instead of ivory.

steps.text: Stir in the ginger and garlic pastes and fry 2 minutes until the raw smell lifts.
Add the chicken and turn it in the masala over medium heat for 5 minutes, until it turns opaque but takes no colour.
Take the pan off the heat, stir in the whisked yogurt in three additions, then return to the lowest flame and cook 6–8 minutes, stirring constantly, until the fat separates.
steps.tip: Off the heat, in stages, stirring — that is the whole trick to yogurt not curdling.

steps.text: Stir in the nut paste, coriander powder, fennel powder, mace, white pepper and salt and cook 4 minutes.
Pour in 300ml warm water, cover and simmer very gently 20–25 minutes until the chicken is tender.
Finish with the saffron milk, kewra water and the remaining birista crushed over the top. Rest covered 10 minutes before serving.
steps.tip: The rest is not optional — the gravy tightens and the perfume settles in.

recipes.storage: Keeps 3 days refrigerated and tastes better on day two. Reheat covered on low with a splash of water; boiling will split the yogurt gravy.

recipes.name: Murgh Musallam
recipes.subtitle: a whole chicken stuffed with boiled eggs and simmered in a rich birista and nut gravy

ingredients.qty: 1 whole, about 1.2kg, skinned and slashed to the bone at the thighs and breast

ingredients.note: for the cavity
for birista and the gravy base
colour without heat

ingredients.qty: a good pinch, soaked in 3 tbsp warm milk

ingredients.note: for a softer finish

prepNotes: Marinate the chicken at least 4 hours ahead, or overnight — the slashes must be deep enough for the marinade to reach the bone.
Fry the birista and grind the nut paste before you start cooking; both are needed in quick succession.
Take the chicken out of the fridge an hour before it goes in the pan so it cooks evenly through.

steps.text: Fry 3 of the sliced onions in 4 tbsp ghee over medium heat until deep brown, 14-16 minutes. Drain on paper and let them go crisp, then grind half to a paste with the cashews, almonds and 4 tbsp water.
steps.tip: Cool the birista completely before grinding or the paste turns gluey.

steps.text: Rub the chicken all over and into the slashes with half the ginger-garlic paste, 1 tsp salt and the kashmiri chilli. Whisk the yogurt with the coriander powder and coat the bird. Refrigerate 4 hours.
Push the boiled eggs into the cavity and tie the legs together with kitchen string so the stuffing stays put.
Heat the remaining 2 tbsp ghee in a wide heavy pan and brown the marinated chicken on all sides, 8-10 minutes, turning with two spoons. Lift it out and reserve any marinade left in the bowl.
steps.tip: Handle it by the cavity, not the legs, or the skinned meat tears.

steps.text: In the same pan crackle the bay leaves, cinnamon, cloves and both cardamoms for 30 seconds, then add the remaining sliced onion and cook to soft gold, 7 minutes.

Add the rest of the ginger-garlic paste, fry 2 minutes, then stir in the nut-and-birista paste and the reserved marinade. Bhuno on medium heat 8 minutes, until the gravy thickens and ghee rims the pan.
Pour in the hot water with the mace, nutmeg and salt and bring to a simmer. Lower the chicken in breast-side down, spooning gravy over it.
Cover tightly and cook on the lowest heat 45 minutes, turning the bird once at the halfway mark and basting twice.
steps.tip: A knife into the thickest part of the thigh should meet no resistance and run clear.

steps.text: Uncover, spoon over the cream and saffron milk and cook 5 minutes more to glaze. If you want a browned top, slide the open pan under a hot oven grill for 4 minutes.
Finish with the kewra water, rest 10 minutes, then carve at the table with the remaining crushed birista scattered over.

recipes.storage: The carved chicken keeps 2 days refrigerated in its gravy. Reheat covered on low with a splash of water; the breast dries out in a microwave, so use a pan.

recipes.name: Mutton Kaliya
recipes.subtitle: the everyday turmeric-yellow mutton curry of Lucknow kitchens, lighter and sharper than korma

ingredients.note: shoulder and neck give the best gravy
half mustard oil is common in home kitchens
kaliya is named for its yellow, so do not skimp
ground saunf, the Awadhi backbone

ingredients.qty: a generous pinch, soaked in 2 tbsp warm milk

ingredients.note: added off the heat

prepNotes: Bring the mutton to room temperature 30 minutes before cooking — cold meat seizes and takes longer to tenderise.
Whisk the yogurt with a fork until it is pourable and lump-free. Lumpy yogurt splits the moment it hits the pan.
Soak the saffron in warm milk at least 20 minutes ahead so it bleeds properly.

steps.text: Fry the sliced onion in the ghee over medium heat until evenly deep brown, 12-14 minutes. Lift it out onto paper and reserve.
steps.tip: Pull it out at reddish-brown, not black — burnt birista turns the whole kaliya bitter.

steps.text: In the same ghee add the bay leaf, cinnamon, cloves and both cardamoms. When they swell and smell sweet, about 40 seconds, add the chopped onion and cook to pale gold, 6 minutes.
Stir in the ginger and garlic pastes and fry 2 minutes, until the raw smell goes and the fat looks glossy.
Add the mutton and brown it hard over high heat for 8 minutes, until the pieces are seared on all sides and the pan is dry.
Take the pan off the heat for a minute, then whisk in the yogurt a spoonful at a time, stirring constantly. Return to low heat.
steps.tip: Off the heat and slowly — this is the only step where a kaliya can curdle.

steps.text: Add the turmeric, coriander, chilli, fennel and dry ginger powders with the salt. Bhuno over medium heat for 8-10 minutes, until the ghee separates and pools at the edges.
steps.tip: The colour shifts from pale to a deep, clear yellow when the masala is done.

steps.text: Pour in the hot water, bring to a boil, then cover and simmer on the lowest heat for 50-60 minutes, stirring every 15 minutes, until the meat gives to a spoon.
Crush the reserved birista between your palms and stir it in with the ground mace. Simmer uncovered 5 minutes to thicken.
Take off the heat, stir in the saffron milk and kewra water, cover and rest 10 minutes before serving with sheermal or plain rice.

recipes.storage: Keeps 3 days refrigerated and tastes better on day two. Reheat gently over low heat with 3-4 tbsp water; never boil hard or the yogurt gravy will split.

recipes.name: Mutton Korma
recipes.subtitle: slow-braised mutton in a dark, nut-thickened yogurt gravy scented with black cardamom

ingredients.qty: 750g bone-in shoulder and shank, in large pieces

ingredients.note: the smoky backbone of this korma

ingredients.qty: a pinch in 2 tbsp warm milk

prepNotes: Marinate the mutton in the whisked yogurt with the ginger and garlic pastes for 2 hours refrigerated, then bring to room temperature before cooking.
Soak the cashew, melon seeds and poppy seeds together in hot water for 30 minutes so they grind to a paste with no grit.
Set aside 90 minutes of unhurried stove time. Mutton korma cannot be rushed with high heat.

steps.text: Fry the sliced onions in 4 tbsp ghee over medium heat until deep brown, 12–14 minutes. Drain the birista and reserve the ghee.
steps.tip: Even browning matters more than speed — stir every minute after the eighth.

steps.text: Grind the soaked seeds and nuts with two-thirds of the birista and 5 tbsp water to a smooth paste.
Heat the reserved ghee with the remaining 2 tbsp, add the bay leaves, black and green cardamom, cloves and cinnamon and let them crackle 40 seconds.
Lift the mutton out of the marinade and brown it in batches over high heat, 4 minutes a batch. Return all of it to the pan.
Lower the flame, pour in the leftover yogurt marinade a ladle at a time and stir without stopping for 8 minutes until the fat rims the pan.
steps.tip: Never cover the pan while yogurt is still raw — trapped steam splits it.

steps.text: Add the coriander powder, kashmiri chilli, mace and salt and bhuno for 5 minutes, splashing in a little hot water each time it catches.
Stir in the nut paste and cook 4 minutes until it darkens a shade and smells toasted.
Add 500ml hot water, bring to a bare simmer, cover tightly and cook 60–70 minutes until the meat pulls off the bone.
steps.tip: A bare simmer, one bubble at a time. A rolling boil toughens the meat and thins the gravy.

steps.text: Uncover and reduce 5 minutes if the gravy is looser than a pouring cream.
Finish with saffron milk, kewra water, grated nutmeg and the reserved birista. Rest covered 10 minutes.

recipes.storage: Improves overnight. Keeps 4 days refrigerated or 2 months frozen. Reheat gently on the stove with a splash of water, never in a hard boil.

recipes.name: Muzaffar
recipes.subtitle: saffron-yellow fine vermicelli fried in ghee and glazed with syrup, khoya and slivered nuts

ingredients.note: grated paneer is a poor but workable stand-in

ingredients.qty: a good pinch, soaked in 2 tbsp warm milk

ingredients.note: for the saffron

prepNotes: Soak the saffron in warm milk at least 20 minutes ahead so the colour is deep, not streaky.
Sliver the nuts and have them ready; once the vermicelli is roasted the dish moves fast.
Use fine seviyan, not thick noodles — the strands should stay separate at the end, never mushy.

steps.text: Warm 3 tbsp ghee in a kadhai on low heat and add the broken vermicelli. Roast 6-8 minutes, stirring constantly, until it is a deep even brown and smells toasty.
steps.tip: Constant stirring and low heat. Vermicelli goes from brown to burnt in about fifteen seconds.

steps.text: Tip the roasted vermicelli onto a plate so it stops cooking.
In the same pan bring the sugar and water to a boil and cook 4 minutes, until the syrup is slightly sticky between finger and thumb but nowhere near thread stage.
Stir the saffron milk and ground cardamom into the syrup.
Add the roasted vermicelli to the simmering syrup, stir once, cover and cook on the lowest heat 6-8 minutes, until the strands are soft and the syrup is almost gone.
steps.tip: Do not stir while it cooks or the strands break into mush.

steps.text: Fry the almonds, pistachios and raisins in the remaining 2 tbsp ghee in a small pan for 90 seconds, until the nuts are gold and the raisins swell.
Uncover the vermicelli, scatter over the crumbled khoya and half the fried nuts, and fold through gently with a fork.
Sprinkle the kewra water, cover off the heat and rest 5 minutes.
Serve warm, topped with the remaining nuts and raisins.

recipes.storage: Keeps 3 days refrigerated in a covered box. Reheat covered on low with 1 tbsp milk to loosen it, or eat cold — many in Lucknow prefer it that way.

recipes.name: Nargisi Kofta
recipes.subtitle: boiled eggs sheathed in spiced mutton mince, fried and halved into a korma gravy

ingredients.note: binds the mince around the egg
one for the kofta, two for birista

ingredients.qty: a pinch in 2 tbsp warm milk

prepNotes: Boil the eggs 9 minutes, cool under running water and peel carefully. A torn white makes a kofta that splits in the oil.
Cook and grind the mince at least an hour ahead and chill it — cold mince wraps cleanly, warm mince slides off.
Have the gravy finished and waiting before you fry. The koftas go in only at the last moment.

steps.text: Simmer the mince with the drained chana dal, one sliced onion, ginger and garlic pastes, salt and 150ml water until dry, about 20 minutes.
steps.tip: Cook it down until the pan is genuinely dry. Damp mince will not seal around the egg.

steps.text: Cool, then grind to a stiff paste and knead in the roasted besan, green chilli, chopped coriander and half the garam masala. Refrigerate 45 minutes.
Divide into 6, flatten each into a disc on your wet palm and wrap it around an egg, sealing every seam.
steps.tip: Hunt for cracks with your fingertips before frying. One gap and the kofta bursts.

steps.text: Deep fry two at a time in medium-hot oil, turning, until an even deep brown, 3–4 minutes. Drain and set aside.
For the gravy, fry the two remaining sliced onions in 2 tbsp ghee until deep brown, 12 minutes. Drain, cool and grind with the soaked cashews and 4 tbsp water.
Heat the remaining ghee with the cardamom, cinnamon and cloves for 30 seconds, then add the onion-cashew paste and cook 5 minutes.
Off the heat, whisk in the yogurt in three additions, return to a low flame and stir 6 minutes until the fat separates.
steps.tip: Adding cold yogurt to a hot pan in one go is how this gravy splits.

steps.text: Add the coriander powder, kashmiri chilli, mace, remaining garam masala and salt and cook 3 minutes, then pour in 350ml warm water and simmer 12 minutes.
Halve each kofta lengthways with a sharp knife so the egg shows, and lay them cut side up in the gravy.
Spoon the gravy over, add the saffron milk, cover and rest off the heat 5 minutes before serving.
steps.tip: Do not simmer the koftas in the gravy — they go soggy and fall apart.

recipes.storage: The gravy keeps 3 days refrigerated on its own. Store koftas separately and reheat them 5 minutes in a hot oven, then combine at the table. Do not freeze.

recipes.name: Nihari
recipes.subtitle: Overnight shank stew, thickened with wheat flour and finished with ginger and lime

ingredients.qty: 1kg shank on the bone, with marrow

ingredients.note: the traditional thickener

prepNotes: Nihari comes from nahar, meaning morning: it was cooked overnight and eaten at dawn. The long, low cook is not optional — it is what turns shank into something spoonable.
Shank with marrow bones is the cut. Boneless meat makes a curry, not nihari.

steps.text: Brown the sliced onion in ghee, then add the ginger and garlic pastes and cook until the raw smell goes.
Add the powdered spices with a splash of water so they do not scorch, then the mutton. Turn it in the masala over high heat until sealed.
Add 2 litres of water and the whole spices. Bring to a boil, then drop to the barest simmer, cover, and cook 4-5 hours until the meat slides off the bone.
steps.tip: A trembling surface, not a rolling boil. Boiling makes the meat stringy.

steps.text: Whisk the atta into a cup of cold water until perfectly smooth and stir it into the pot. Simmer 30 minutes more, stirring often, until the gravy coats a spoon.
steps.tip: Cold water and hard whisking, or you will get lumps you cannot remove.

steps.text: Rest off the heat 20 minutes; the fat will rise. Do not skim it — that layer is the point.
Serve with julienned ginger, green chilli, coriander and a hard squeeze of lemon at the table.

recipes.storage: Improves for two days refrigerated and is arguably better on day two. Reheat gently with hot water. Freezes 2 months.

recipes.name: Shahi Tukda
recipes.subtitle: ghee-fried bread soaked in saffron syrup under a blanket of thick rabri

ingredients.qty: 8 slices of white bread, crusts cut off
ingredients.note: day-old bread fries crisper than fresh
for the rabri; there is no shortcut to reducing it
thickens the rabri faster

ingredients.qty: 150g for the syrup, plus 3 tbsp for the rabri
a generous pinch, steeped in 2 tbsp warm milk

prepNotes: Reduce the milk for the rabri first — it takes 45 minutes and cannot be hurried.
Use day-old bread and leave the slices uncovered for an hour so they dry out; fresh bread soaks up ghee and goes soggy.
Steep the saffron in warm milk for 20 minutes.

steps.text: Simmer the milk in a wide heavy pan over medium-low heat, scraping the cream back in from the sides every few minutes, until reduced to about a third, 40–45 minutes.
steps.tip: A wide pan, not a tall one. Surface area is what reduces milk.

steps.text: Stir in the grated khoya, 3 tbsp sugar, half the saffron milk and half the cardamom powder and cook 5 minutes more. Set the rabri aside to cool a little.
Meanwhile boil the 150g sugar with 150ml water for 5 minutes to a thin one-string syrup, then stir in the remaining saffron milk and the rose water.
steps.tip: Thin syrup. A thick one turns the bread to candy.

steps.text: Cut each bread slice into two triangles.
Fry them in ghee over medium heat until deep golden and crisp on both sides, 2 minutes a side, adding ghee as needed. Drain on paper.
steps.tip: Fry to properly crisp — bread that is only pale will collapse in the syrup.

steps.text: Dip each fried triangle into the warm syrup for 5 seconds a side and lift it straight out onto a serving plate.
steps.tip: Five seconds, no more. Any longer and it disintegrates.

steps.text: Arrange the soaked bread in a single overlapping layer and spoon the warm rabri over the top.
Scatter with pistachios, almonds and the remaining cardamom powder.
Chill 1 hour before serving so the rabri sets and the bread softens through.

recipes.storage: Keeps 2 days refrigerated, covered. It is served chilled or at room temperature, never reheated — the bread turns to mush. Assemble on the day you plan to eat it.

recipes.name: Shami Kebab
recipes.subtitle: dense little mutton and chana dal patties, smooth inside and crisp at the edge

ingredients.note: the binder — nothing else does the same job

ingredients.qty: 1 medium quartered for the boil, 1 small very finely chopped for the mix

ingredients.note: helps the patties hold when frying
to squeeze at the table
neutral oil works but tastes flatter

prepNotes: Soak the chana dal 1 hour in warm water. Undersoaked dal stays gritty and the kebab will crumble.
The cooked mince must be bone dry before grinding — any moisture and the patties fall apart in the pan.
Chill the shaped kebabs 30 minutes before frying. They firm up and turn far more easily.

steps.text: Pressure cook the mutton, drained dal, quartered onion, garlic, ginger, whole chillies, black cardamom, green cardamom, cinnamon, cloves, peppercorns, salt and 250ml water for 5 whistles, about 20 minutes.
steps.tip: In a pan instead, allow 50 minutes covered on low.

steps.text: Open the lid and boil hard, stirring, until every trace of liquid has gone and the mix looks dry and sandy, 8–10 minutes.
steps.tip: This is the step people skip. Wet mince equals kebabs that disintegrate.

steps.text: Cool completely, then pick out the cinnamon stick and black cardamom shell and grind the rest to a smooth, tight paste with no added water.
Knead in the finely chopped onion, green chilli, coriander, mint, garam masala and the beaten egg. Taste for salt now.
Divide into 12 and shape into flat discs 5cm across and 1.5cm thick. Refrigerate 30 minutes.
Heat 2 tbsp ghee on a tawa over medium heat and lay in the kebabs without crowding.
Fry 3–4 minutes a side until a deep brown crust forms, adding the remaining ghee as you turn.
steps.tip: Turn once only, with a thin spatula. Fiddling breaks them.

steps.text: Drain on paper, rest 2 minutes and serve hot with lemon wedges and sliced onion.

recipes.storage: Cooked kebabs keep 3 days refrigerated and reheat well on a dry tawa over low heat. The raw ground mix freezes for a month; thaw fully before shaping.

recipes.name: Sheermal
recipes.subtitle: slightly sweet saffron-milk flatbread, soft as brioche, brushed with ghee

ingredients.note: the shir in sheermal — this is what makes it
helps the crumb stay soft
traditionally sheermal is yeast-leavened; soda with yogurt gives a similar soft crumb in less time

ingredients.qty: a generous pinch, steeped in 3 tbsp warm milk

prepNotes: Steep the saffron in warm milk for at least 20 minutes so it gives up its full colour.
The dough must rest 1 hour covered at room temperature. Skipping the rest gives a tough, cracker-like bread.
Preheat the oven with the tray inside for 20 minutes; sheermal wants immediate bottom heat.

steps.text: Dissolve the sugar and salt in the warm milk and stir in the yogurt.
steps.tip: Warm, not hot — hot milk cooks the yogurt into lumps.

steps.text: Mix the maida with the baking soda, rub in 60g of the melted ghee until it looks like breadcrumbs, then add half the saffron milk.
Add the milk mixture gradually and knead 10 minutes to a soft, smooth, slightly sticky dough.
steps.tip: Softer than a chapati dough. Resist adding extra flour.

steps.text: Cover with a damp cloth and rest 1 hour at room temperature.
Knock back, divide into 8 and roll each into a disc 15cm across and 5mm thick. Prick all over with a fork.
steps.tip: The fork holes stop it ballooning into a puri.

steps.text: Bake at 220C on a preheated tray for 6–7 minutes, until the surface is set and just speckled.
Pull the tray out, brush each bread generously with the remaining saffron milk and melted ghee, and return for 3 minutes.
steps.tip: The saffron glaze goes on partway through, not at the start, or it scorches.

steps.text: Dust with cardamom powder, stack under a cloth and serve warm with korma or kebabs.

recipes.storage: Keeps 2 days wrapped in a cloth at room temperature, or 5 days refrigerated. Revive on a hot tawa for 30 seconds a side; the microwave makes them chewy.

recipes.name: Ulte Tawe Ka Paratha
recipes.subtitle: wafer-thin layered paratha cooked on the back of an upturned tawa

ingredients.note: a little wholemeal gives the paratha some backbone

ingredients.qty: 6 tbsp, melted, plus more for cooking

prepNotes: The dough needs 45 minutes covered at room temperature. Unrested dough will not roll thin enough and springs back.
You need an upturned kadhai or a heavy iron tawa turned convex side up — the curve is what lets the bread drape and cook evenly.
Melt the ghee for laminating and keep it liquid but not hot beside your rolling board.

steps.text: Mix the maida, atta, salt and sugar, rub in 2 tbsp of the melted ghee, then bring together with the warm milk and enough warm water to make a soft dough.
Knead 10 minutes until smooth and elastic, then cover with a damp cloth and rest 45 minutes.
steps.tip: Ten minutes of kneading is what builds the stretch. Under-kneaded dough tears when you roll it thin.

steps.text: Divide into 8 and roll one ball into a 20cm disc.
Brush it all over with melted ghee, dust lightly with dry maida, then cut a slit from centre to edge and roll it tightly into a cone.
steps.tip: Ghee then flour, in that order — that pairing is what separates the layers.

steps.text: Press the cone down onto its point into a flat pastry and rest 10 minutes. Repeat with the rest.
Roll each pastry out to a very thin disc, 22–24cm across, working from the centre outwards.
steps.tip: Light pressure and lots of small strokes. Leaning on the pin squashes the layers together.

steps.text: Set the tawa upside down over medium heat and let it get properly hot, 4 minutes.
Drape a paratha over the convex surface and cook 60–90 seconds until the underside is spotted brown and it lifts freely.
Flip with tongs, brush with ghee and cook 60 seconds more, pressing the edges down onto the metal.
Crush the hot paratha lightly between your palms to open the layers and serve at once with galouti or korma.
steps.tip: That crumpling is the point of the whole exercise — do it while it is too hot to be comfortable.

recipes.storage: Best within minutes of cooking. The rolled, un-cooked pastries keep a day refrigerated between sheets of paper. Cooked parathas go leathery in the fridge; refresh on a hot tawa with a little ghee.

recipes.name: Warqi Paratha
recipes.subtitle: a many-layered flaky paratha that shatters into thin leaves, the Lucknow bread for korma

ingredients.note: plain flour; atta will not give the leaves
2 in the dough, 4 for layering and cooking
beaten with ghee into the layering paste, or sata

prepNotes: The layering paste (sata) is 3 tbsp soft ghee beaten with the rice flour until it is white and fluffy — do this first and keep it at room temperature.
Rest the dough a full 30 minutes covered with a damp cloth. Unrested dough springs back and the layers tear.
Work in a cool kitchen if you can; warm ghee melts into the dough instead of separating the leaves.

steps.text: Rub 2 tbsp ghee into the maida with the salt and sugar until the flour looks like damp breadcrumbs and holds when squeezed.
Add the warm milk, then water a little at a time, and knead 6-8 minutes to a soft, smooth dough that is slightly stickier than chapati dough.
Cover with a damp cloth and rest 30 minutes.
Divide into 4 balls. Roll one out into a thin round about 22cm across, as even as you can get it.
Spread 1 heaped tsp of the ghee-and-rice-flour paste right to the edges, then pleat the round into a narrow fan, folding it back and forth in 1.5cm concertina folds.
steps.tip: Spread the paste thin and to the very edge — bare patches glue the layers shut.

steps.text: Stretch the pleated strip gently, then coil it into a spiral like a snail shell and tuck the end underneath. Rest 10 minutes.
Press the coil flat with your palm and roll it out to about 15cm, using the lightest pressure you can. Repeat with the rest.
steps.tip: Roll from the centre outwards and stop while it still looks thick — pressing hard crushes the layers you just built.

steps.text: Cook on a medium-hot tawa 1.5 minutes a side until pale brown spots appear, then brush with ghee and press the edges down with a cloth as it puffs.
Lift off and immediately clap the paratha between your palms once — the leaves separate and fan out.

recipes.storage: Best within an hour. Cooked parathas keep a day wrapped in a cloth in an airtight box; revive on a dry tawa for 40 seconds a side. The dough keeps 24 hours refrigerated.

recipes.name: Zarda
recipes.subtitle: saffron sweet rice studded with nuts and raisins, served at the end of a dastarkhwan

ingredients.qty: a generous pinch, steeped in 3 tbsp warm milk
ingredients.note: the colour comes from saffron, not food dye

prepNotes: Soak the rice 30 minutes and drain it well. Aged long-grain basmati holds its shape; new-crop rice turns to porridge.
Steep the saffron in warm milk for 20 minutes before you start.
Have the nuts fried and drained before the rice goes on — the last stage moves quickly.

steps.text: Fry the almonds, pistachios, cashews and coconut in 2 tbsp ghee until just gold, 2 minutes, then the raisins for 20 seconds until they puff. Drain and set aside.
steps.tip: Raisins go in last and come out fast; they burn in seconds.

steps.text: Boil 1.2 litres of water with the salt, half the saffron milk, the cardamom and cloves.
Add the drained rice and cook uncovered for 6–7 minutes, until the grains are 80 percent done and still firm at the core.
steps.tip: Bite one: it should give but leave a chalky centre. It finishes cooking in the syrup.

steps.text: Drain thoroughly in a colander and leave 5 minutes to steam dry.
In a heavy pan melt the remaining 3 tbsp ghee, add the sugar and 100ml water and stir until it dissolves into a thin syrup, 3 minutes.
Fold the drained rice gently into the syrup with the remaining saffron milk, using a flat spoon and lifting rather than stirring.
steps.tip: Stirring smashes the grains. Lift and fold from underneath.

steps.text: Cover tightly, put a heavy lid or a weight on top and cook on the lowest possible heat for 15 minutes.
Uncover: the syrup should be absorbed and the grains separate and glossy. If wet, cook uncovered 3 minutes more.
Scatter over the fried nuts, raisins, crumbled khoya and kewra water, cover again and rest 10 minutes off the heat before serving warm.

recipes.storage: Keeps 3 days refrigerated. Reheat covered with a teaspoon of water and a knob of ghee, on low or in short bursts in the microwave. It stiffens when cold and loosens as it warms.

recipes.name: Aloo Posto
recipes.subtitle: potatoes cooked down in a nutty poppy seed paste, mild and quietly rich

ingredients.note: posto — the whole point of the dish

ingredients.qty: 4, 2 ground with the posto and 2 slit

ingredients.note: kalonji
rounds off the bitterness of the poppy seeds

prepNotes: Soak the poppy seeds in just-boiled water for 30 minutes — dry seeds will never grind smooth.
Drain the seeds well before grinding, then blend with 2 green chillies and 4 tbsp water to a thick, pale paste.
Cut the potatoes and keep them in cold water so they do not brown while the paste is going.

steps.text: Heat the mustard oil in a kadhai until it smokes, then take it off the heat for 30 seconds to lose its raw bite.
steps.tip: Bengali cooking almost always starts with mustard oil taken to smoking point.

steps.text: Return to medium heat, add the nigella seeds and let them sputter for 10 seconds.
Drain the potatoes, pat dry, and add them with the turmeric and salt. Fry 6-7 minutes, turning, until the edges are pale gold.
steps.tip: Dry potatoes fry; wet potatoes steam and go mushy.

steps.text: Pour in 180ml water, cover, and simmer 10-12 minutes until a knife slides through the potato with slight resistance.
Stir in the poppy seed paste and the slit green chillies. Cook uncovered on low for 6-8 minutes.
steps.tip: Keep the heat low — posto catches and turns bitter over a high flame.

steps.text: The gravy is ready when it clings to the potatoes and you can see oil at the edge of the pan.
Add the sugar, check the salt, and finish with the remaining 1 tbsp raw mustard oil off the heat.
steps.tip: That last spoon of raw oil is what makes it taste Bengali rather than merely mild.

steps.text: Rest 5 minutes before serving with plain rice.

recipes.storage: Keeps 2 days refrigerated. Reheat gently with 2 tbsp water; the posto thickens hard as it cools.

recipes.name: Basanti Pulao
recipes.subtitle: sweet saffron-yellow ghee rice studded with cashews and raisins

ingredients.note: gobindobhog is traditional; basmati works if you shorten the cooking by 3 minutes
this, not the saffron, is what makes it yellow

ingredients.qty: a large pinch, soaked in 2 tbsp warm water

prepNotes: Wash the rice gently in three changes of water until it runs clear, then drain and spread it on a cloth for 30 minutes until the grains are dry to the touch.
Toss the dried rice with 2 tbsp of the ghee, the turmeric and 1 tsp salt and leave it 30 minutes — this coats each grain and keeps them separate.
Have the water hot on the side. Adding cold water to hot rice makes it break.

steps.text: Heat the remaining 2 tbsp ghee in a heavy pan and fry the cashews until golden, about 90 seconds. Lift out.
steps.tip: Cashews go from gold to burnt in about ten seconds. Watch them.

steps.text: Fry the raisins in the same ghee for 20 seconds until they swell, then lift them out too.
Add the bay leaves, cardamom, cinnamon and cloves and let them puff for 20 seconds.
Add the grated ginger and stir for 30 seconds.
Tip in the marinated rice and fry very gently for 3 minutes, folding rather than stirring.
steps.tip: Turmeric-coated rice grains are fragile. A flat spoon and slow folds keep them whole.

steps.text: Pour in 500ml hot water with the sugar, the saffron and its soaking water, and the rest of the salt.
Bring to a boil, then cover tightly and cook on the lowest possible heat for 12 minutes.
steps.tip: Do not lift the lid. Every peek lets out the steam that is cooking the top layer.

steps.text: Turn off the heat and leave it covered and undisturbed for 10 minutes.
Uncover, fork through the fried cashews and raisins, and serve with kosha mangsho or a dry vegetable.

recipes.storage: Keeps 2 days refrigerated. Reheat covered with 2 tbsp water in a pan over low heat, or steam it — the microwave dries the grains out.

recipes.name: Begun Bhaja
recipes.subtitle: thick eggplant slices fried until the edges go dark and lacy

ingredients.qty: 1 large round variety (about 400g), cut into 1cm rounds
ingredients.note: the fat purple globe kind, not the slim ones
helps the surface caramelise
for a light crust; leave out for the plainer version

prepNotes: Rub the eggplant rounds with the salt, turmeric, chilli powder and sugar and leave 20 minutes — they will bead with water.
Blot the rounds dry with a cloth just before frying, otherwise the oil will spit.
If you are using the rice flour, dust it on at the last moment so it does not go gummy.

steps.text: Heat the mustard oil in a wide tawa until it smokes, then lower the heat to medium.
steps.tip: Smoking the mustard oil first is not optional — raw mustard oil tastes acrid.

steps.text: Lay in the eggplant rounds in a single layer, leaving space between them.
steps.tip: Crowding drops the oil temperature and you get soggy slices instead of crisp ones.

steps.text: Fry 3-4 minutes without touching them, until the underside is deep brown and the edge looks frilled.
Turn once with a flat spatula and fry the second side 3 minutes.
steps.tip: Turn only once. Every extra flip makes the slice absorb more oil.

steps.text: Press the centre lightly — it should give completely, with no firm core left.
Lift onto kitchen paper and fry the next batch, adding a little more oil if the pan looks dry.
Serve immediately alongside hot rice and dal, while the edges are still crisp.

recipes.storage: Eat within the hour — they go limp on standing and do not reheat well. Do not refrigerate.

recipes.name: Bengali Alur Dom
recipes.subtitle: baby potatoes sealed in a tangy yogurt and ginger gravy, the standard partner to luchi

ingredients.note: 1 tsp for the tempering, 1/2 tsp dry-roasted for the finish
one for the tempering, one dry-roasted for the finish
use compounded-free hing to keep the dish gluten-free

prepNotes: Boil the potatoes only until a fork goes in with slight resistance, then peel and prick them all over with a fork so the gravy gets inside.
Dry-roast 1/2 tsp cumin seeds and one dried chilli in a pan until they smell toasty, then grind them to a coarse powder. This bhaja moshla goes in at the very end and is what makes it taste Bengali.
Whisk the yogurt smooth and leave it at room temperature for 20 minutes before you begin.

steps.text: Heat the mustard oil to smoking point in a kadhai and let it settle off the heat for 30 seconds.
Fry the boiled potatoes with 1/4 tsp turmeric and a pinch of salt over medium heat for 6 to 7 minutes, until the skins are blistered and gold all over, then lift them out.
steps.tip: Dry the potatoes properly first or they will spit and refuse to colour.

steps.text: Add the bay leaf, 1 tsp cumin seeds and one dried chilli to the oil and let them crackle for 20 seconds, then stir in the asafoetida.
Fry the ginger paste for 1 minute, until it loses its raw smell.
Add the pureed tomato with the remaining turmeric, kashmiri chilli, cumin and coriander powders and cook 6 minutes, until the oil separates cleanly at the sides.
Pull the pan off the heat, beat in the whisked yogurt, then set it back on the lowest flame and cook 3 minutes without boiling.
steps.tip: If it looks grainy, take it off and whisk hard; it will come back together.

steps.text: Return the potatoes with the sugar, salt and slit chillies and turn them in the masala for 3 minutes so every one is coated.
Add the water, bring to a simmer, then cover tightly and cook on the lowest heat for 12 minutes.
steps.tip: A tight lid is the point of dum: the potatoes finish in trapped steam, not in liquid.

steps.text: Uncover, raise the heat and reduce for 3 minutes until the gravy clings to the potatoes rather than pooling.
Stir through the garam masala, the ghee and the roasted bhaja moshla, cover and rest 5 minutes before serving.

recipes.storage: Keeps 3 days refrigerated and tastes better on day two. Reheat on low with a splash of water and add the bhaja moshla fresh if you have it.

recipes.name: Bengali Ghugni
recipes.subtitle: white peas stewed soft with fried coconut slivers and a dust of roasted spice

ingredients.qty: 1 large finely chopped, plus 1/2 finely chopped raw for the top

ingredients.note: narkel kuchi, fried in the oil first
1 tsp for the tempering, 1/2 tsp dry-roasted for the finish
one for the tempering, one dry-roasted for the finish
or a squeeze of lemon at the table
in the soaking water, for peas that refuse to soften

prepNotes: Soak the white peas overnight in plenty of water with 1/4 tsp baking soda. Old peas can take a full 12 hours and will still be stubborn without it.

Pressure-cook the drained peas with the turmeric, salt and 500ml water for 3 whistles, then let the pressure fall on its own. They should be soft enough to crush between two fingers but not shapeless.
Dry-roast 1/2 tsp cumin seeds and one dried chilli until they smell toasty and grind them coarse. This bhaja moshla is sprinkled over at the end and is not optional if you want the real thing.

steps.text: Heat the mustard oil in a kadhai to smoking point, then take it off the heat for 30 seconds.
Fry the coconut slivers over medium heat for about 90 seconds, until they turn light brown at the edges, and lift them out.
steps.tip: They colour suddenly at the end. Take them out a shade paler than you want.

steps.text: Fry the diced potato in the same oil for 5 minutes until golden, then set aside.
Add the bay leaf, 1 tsp cumin seeds and one dried chilli and let them crackle for 20 seconds.
Add the chopped onion and fry for 8 minutes, stirring, until deep gold at the edges.
Stir in the ginger paste and cook 1 minute, then add the tomato with the chilli, cumin and coriander powders and cook 6 minutes until the oil separates.
steps.tip: Mash the tomato against the pan as it goes; you want no pieces left, only masala.

steps.text: Tip in the cooked peas with their liquid, the fried potato, the sugar and salt, and the remaining 100ml water.
Simmer uncovered for 15 minutes, crushing a ladleful of peas against the side of the pan to thicken the gravy.
steps.tip: Ghugni should be thick enough to sit on a spoon, not pour off it.

steps.text: Stir in the tamarind pulp and slit chillies and cook 2 minutes more, then check the salt.
Serve in bowls topped with the fried coconut, raw chopped onion, coriander, a dusting of bhaja moshla and garam masala, with lemon wedges alongside.

recipes.storage: Keeps 3 days refrigerated and thickens as it sits. Reheat with 3 to 4 tbsp water and add the coconut, raw onion and bhaja moshla fresh each time.

recipes.name: Chingri Bhapa
recipes.subtitle: prawns steamed in mustard, coconut and green chilli until just set and sweet

ingredients.qty: 500g medium, shelled and deveined, tails on

ingredients.note: soaked, then ground
soaked, then ground

ingredients.qty: 5, three for the paste and two whole

ingredients.note: for a rounder, milder version

ingredients.qty: 3 tbsp for the paste, plus water for the steamer

prepNotes: Soak the mustard seeds and poppy seeds together for 20 minutes in warm water with a green chilli and a pinch of salt, then grind fine. Under-soaked mustard tastes bitter and grits between the teeth.
Devein the prawns and pat them completely dry, then rub with 1/4 tsp turmeric and a little salt for 10 minutes.
Set up a tight-lidded steel tiffin box or a foil-sealed bowl standing in a covered pan of simmering water before you mix anything.

steps.text: Grind the soaked mustard and poppy seeds with three green chillies, the coconut and 3 tbsp water to a smooth paste.
Beat 3 tbsp of the mustard oil into the paste along with the remaining turmeric, the sugar, salt and the coconut milk if using.
steps.tip: The oil must be beaten in, not poured on top, or it will separate during steaming.

steps.text: Fold the prawns through the paste until evenly coated and let them sit 10 minutes.
Spread the prawns in a single layer in the tiffin box, scrape in every bit of paste, and tuck in the two whole chillies.
Spoon the last tablespoon of raw mustard oil over the surface and close the lid tightly.
Stand the box in a pan with water a third of the way up its sides, cover, and steam on medium for 15 minutes.
steps.tip: Prawns go rubbery fast. Fifteen minutes is enough; twenty is too many.

steps.text: Turn off the heat and leave the box shut for 5 minutes to finish in its own steam.
Open away from your face and serve immediately with hot plain rice.

recipes.storage: Best on the day. It keeps 24 hours refrigerated; reheat by steaming the closed box for 4 minutes, never in a pan, which toughens the prawns.

recipes.name: Chingri Malai Curry
recipes.subtitle: prawns in a sweet cardamom-scented coconut milk gravy

ingredients.qty: 500g large, shelled and deveined, heads left on if you have them
1 large, ground to a smooth paste

ingredients.note: the sweetness is characteristic, not a mistake

prepNotes: Rub the prawns with 1/2 tsp turmeric and 1/2 tsp salt and rest 10 minutes, no longer — salt draws water out of prawns fast.
Shake the tin of coconut milk hard, or whisk the thick and thin parts together, before measuring.
Grind the onion without water so the paste fries rather than stews.

steps.text: Heat the mustard oil to smoking, cool for 30 seconds, then sear the prawns 45 seconds a side until they just turn pink at the edges. Lift them out immediately.
steps.tip: They are not cooked through at this point and should not be. Prawns need 90 seconds total in the whole recipe.

steps.text: Add the bay leaves, cardamom, cinnamon and cloves to the same oil and let them puff for 20 seconds.
Add the onion paste and fry 7-8 minutes on medium until it turns pale gold and the oil begins to separate.
steps.tip: Do not brown it. This gravy should stay ivory-white, not go tan.

steps.text: Stir in the ginger paste, the remaining turmeric and the kashmiri chilli and cook 1 minute.
Pour in the coconut milk with the sugar and salt, stirring as you go.
Simmer on low, uncovered, for 6-7 minutes until the gravy coats the back of a spoon.
steps.tip: Keep it below a rolling boil or the coconut milk will separate into grains and oil.

steps.text: Return the prawns with the slit green chillies and cook exactly 2 minutes.
steps.tip: The moment a prawn curls into a tight O it is overdone. A loose C is right.

steps.text: Turn off the heat, stir in the ghee and garam masala, and cover for 5 minutes before serving with plain rice.

recipes.storage: Keeps 1 day refrigerated. Reheat gently over low heat only until warm — reheating hard makes the prawns rubbery and splits the coconut milk.

recipes.name: Cholar Dal
recipes.subtitle: bengal gram simmered sweet-spiced with coconut slivers and raisins

ingredients.qty: 4 tbsp fresh, cut into small thin slivers

ingredients.note: cholar dal is meant to be faintly sweet

prepNotes: Rinse the chana dal in three changes of water, then soak 1 hour — it cooks more evenly and holds its shape.
Fry the coconut slivers in 1 tbsp of the ghee until golden and keep them aside; they go in at the end so they stay crisp.
Have the whole spices measured into one small bowl — the tempering takes under a minute.

steps.text: Drain the soaked dal and pressure cook with 700ml water, the turmeric and half the salt for 2 whistles, then let the pressure drop naturally.
steps.tip: You want the grains soft but still individually visible, not collapsed into a puree.

steps.text: Open the cooker and mash lightly against the side with a spoon — about a quarter of the dal, no more.
Keep it on low heat while you make the tempering.
Heat the remaining 2 tbsp ghee in a small pan. Add the bay leaves, dried red chillies, cinnamon, cardamom and cloves and let them swell for 20 seconds.
steps.tip: The cardamom pods puffing up is your cue that the spices have given their oil.

steps.text: Add the cumin seeds and grated ginger and fry 20 seconds until fragrant.
Pour the whole tempering into the dal, stir, and simmer 8 minutes uncovered.
Add the sugar and raisins and cook another 3 minutes until the raisins plump.
Stir in the garam masala and most of the fried coconut. Check the salt.
steps.tip: Taste for the sugar-salt balance here — it should read sweet first, then savoury.

steps.text: Scatter the last of the coconut over the top and serve hot with luchi.

recipes.storage: Keeps 3 days refrigerated. It thickens considerably; loosen with hot water and re-warm gently on the stove.

recipes.name: Dhokar Dalna
recipes.subtitle: diamonds of fried chana dal cake simmered in a gingery potato gravy

ingredients.qty: 3, 2 ground into the dal paste and 1 slit

ingredients.note: for a gluten-free dish use compounded-free hing

prepNotes: Soak the chana dal 5 hours or overnight, then drain it thoroughly.
Grind the drained dal with 2 green chillies and 1 tbsp of the ginger to a coarse, sandy paste using as little water as possible — a wet paste will never set.
Oil a plate or tray before you start cooking the dal; the mixture has to be spread while it is still hot.
The cake must cool completely, at least 30 minutes, before you cut and fry it.

steps.text: Heat 2 tbsp mustard oil in a kadhai, add 1/2 tsp cumin seeds, the nigella and half the asafoetida, and let them crackle for 15 seconds.
Add the dal paste with 1/2 tsp turmeric and salt. Stir constantly over medium heat for 10-12 minutes.
steps.tip: It is done when the paste stops sticking to the pan and rolls into a single ball behind the spoon.

steps.text: Tip the hot mixture onto the oiled tray and press it flat to about 1.5cm with the back of a wet spoon. Cool 30 minutes, then cut into diamonds.
steps.tip: Pressing while hot is what makes the dhoka hold together — once it cools it will crack instead.

steps.text: Heat 3 tbsp oil and fry the diamonds in batches, 2-3 minutes a side, until crusted and deep gold, handling them with a flat spatula. Drain and set aside.
In the same pan fry the potato quarters with a pinch of turmeric for 5 minutes until golden. Set aside.
Add the last 1 tbsp oil, the bay leaves, remaining cumin seeds and asafoetida, and crackle 15 seconds.
Add the remaining ginger paste and cook 1 minute, then the tomato puree and all the ground spices.
Fry this masala 6-8 minutes, sprinkling in a tablespoon of water whenever it sticks, until the oil separates at the edges.
steps.tip: This is the bhuna stage and it cannot be hurried — undercooked masala tastes raw and dusty.

steps.text: Add the potatoes, 600ml water, the slit chilli, sugar and salt. Simmer covered 15 minutes until the potato is tender.
Slide in the fried dhoka pieces and simmer uncovered 3-4 minutes only.
steps.tip: Add them at the very end — any longer and they drink the gravy and fall apart.

steps.text: Finish with the garam masala and ghee, rest 5 minutes, and serve with rice.

recipes.storage: The fried dhoka keeps 3 days refrigerated on its own; the gravy keeps 3 days too. Combine and warm through just before serving rather than storing them together.

recipes.name: Dimer Dalna
recipes.subtitle: boiled eggs fried golden then simmered in a spiced potato gravy
prepNotes: Boil the eggs 9 minutes from cold water, then cool them under the tap so the shells come away cleanly.
Prick each peeled egg four or five times with a fork — this lets the masala get past the surface.
Mix the ground spices with 4 tbsp water into a paste before you start; dry powders scorch in hot mustard oil.

steps.text: Heat the mustard oil to smoking in a kadhai, then reduce to medium.
Roll the pricked eggs in 1/2 tsp turmeric and 1/2 tsp salt and fry them 3-4 minutes, turning, until blistered and golden. Lift out.
steps.tip: Keep a lid handy — eggs spit violently in hot oil for the first few seconds.

steps.text: Fry the halved potatoes in the same oil for 6 minutes until browned on the cut sides. Set aside.
Add the bay leaves and cumin seeds to the oil and let them crackle 15 seconds.
Add the chopped onion and fry 8-10 minutes until deep golden brown.
steps.tip: This browning is where the whole flavour of the gravy comes from. Do not stop at pale.

steps.text: Stir in the garlic and ginger and cook 1 minute, then add the tomato and cook 4 minutes until it breaks down.
Add the spice paste and fry 5-6 minutes, splashing in water whenever it catches, until oil pools at the edge.
steps.tip: Oil separating from the masala is the signal to move on — nothing else is.

steps.text: Return the potatoes with 500ml water, the sugar and salt. Simmer covered 15 minutes until tender.
Add the fried eggs and simmer uncovered 5 minutes so they take on colour.
Stir in the garam masala, scatter the coriander leaves, and rest 5 minutes before serving with rice or luchi.

recipes.storage: Keeps 2 days refrigerated. Reheat in a pan with a little water. The eggs firm up in the fridge but soften again on reheating.

recipes.name: Doi Maach
recipes.subtitle: fish poached in whisked yogurt with cardamom and ginger, tangy and pale gold

ingredients.qty: 2 medium, ground to a smooth paste

ingredients.note: for colour without heat

prepNotes: Rub the fish with 1 tsp turmeric and 1 tsp salt and rest 15 minutes.
Take the yogurt out of the fridge an hour ahead and whisk it with a fork until there is not a single lump — cold, lumpy yogurt splits on contact with heat.
Whisk the kashmiri chilli and remaining turmeric into the yogurt now, not into the hot pan later.

steps.text: Heat the mustard oil to smoking, cool it slightly, then fry the fish steaks 2-3 minutes a side until just set. Lift out.
steps.tip: This is a light fry, not a hard one — the fish finishes in the yogurt.

steps.text: Pour off all but 3 tbsp of the oil. Add the bay leaves, cardamom, cinnamon and cloves and let them swell for 20 seconds.
Add the onion paste and fry 8-10 minutes, stirring often, until it is pale gold and no longer smells sharp.
steps.tip: Onion paste spits and catches. Keep the heat at medium and keep the spoon moving.

steps.text: Add the ginger paste and cook 1 minute more.
Take the pan off the heat entirely and let it cool for a full minute.
steps.tip: Adding yogurt to a screaming hot pan is the single reason this dish fails.

steps.text: Add the spiced yogurt a spoonful at a time, stirring continuously, until it is all in and smooth.
Return to the lowest heat and cook 5-6 minutes, stirring in one direction, until the gravy thickens and gloss appears on the surface.
steps.tip: Never let it boil. If it looks like it is about to break, lift the pan off the heat and keep stirring.

steps.text: Add 150ml water, the sugar, salt and slit chillies and bring to the barest simmer.
Slide the fish back in, spoon the gravy over, and cook 5 minutes covered.
Finish with the ghee off the heat and rest 10 minutes before serving with rice.

recipes.storage: Keeps 2 days refrigerated. Reheat over very low heat, stirring — a yogurt gravy will split if it is rushed or microwaved.

recipes.name: Echorer Dalna
recipes.subtitle: green jackfruit simmered in a gingery gravy until it eats like meat

ingredients.note: green, unripe jackfruit only
use compounded-free hing to keep the dish gluten-free
stirred in at the end

prepNotes: Rub your hands, knife and board with mustard oil before cutting the jackfruit. The latex is sticky and does not wash off easily.
Parboil the jackfruit first with 1/2 tsp turmeric and salt: 2 whistles in a pressure cooker, or 15 minutes in an open pan. It should take a fork with slight resistance before it meets the masala.
Drain the parboiled jackfruit thoroughly and let it steam dry for 5 minutes, or it will not brown.

steps.text: Heat the mustard oil in a kadhai to smoking point, then let it cool for 30 seconds.
Fry the quartered potatoes with a pinch of turmeric and salt over medium heat for 6 minutes, until golden on all sides, and set aside.
Fry the drained jackfruit pieces in the same oil for 6 to 8 minutes, turning, until they are patched with brown. Lift them out.
steps.tip: This browning is the whole point of echor. Pale jackfruit stays bland and spongy.

steps.text: Into the remaining oil add the bay leaves, cinnamon, cardamom, cloves and cumin seeds and let them crackle for 20 seconds, then stir in the asafoetida.
Add the ginger paste and fry for 1 minute, until it stops smelling raw.
