recipes.subtitle: sunday mutton simmered into a purée of four dals and gourds, sour and gently hot

ingredients.qty: 700g, shoulder on the bone, cut into 4cm pieces
ingredients.note: bone is what makes the gravy
the backbone of the dal mix
red pumpkin, for sweetness
the bitter note that defines dhansak
the sliced one is for the brown onion garnish
stand in for dhansak masala

prepNotes: Rinse the four dals together and soak them 45 minutes; they cook far more evenly.
Bring the mutton to room temperature 30 minutes ahead so it browns instead of steaming.
Soak the tamarind in hot water while the dals cook, then squeeze and strain out the fibres.

steps.text: Pressure cook the drained dals with the pumpkin, eggplant, methi leaves, chopped onion, tomato, turmeric and 1 litre of water for 5 whistles, about 20 minutes.
steps.tip: The vegetables melt away — that is the point. Do not keep them chunky.

steps.text: Meanwhile heat 3 tbsp oil in a heavy pan and brown the mutton in two batches over high heat, 5 minutes a batch.
steps.tip: Crowding the pan is the single most common mistake; the meat will grey instead of crusting.

steps.text: Pound the garlic, ginger and green chilli to a coarse paste and fry it in the same pan for 2 minutes, until the raw smell lifts.
Add the cinnamon, cloves, cardamom, black pepper, coriander powder, cumin powder, chilli powder and garam masala and fry 90 seconds, splashing in 2 tbsp water when it catches.
Return the mutton, add 200ml water, cover and simmer 45 minutes until a knife slides into the meat with no resistance.
Cool the dal mixture slightly, fish out any large spice pieces, and blend to a smooth, pourable purée.
steps.tip: Blend it hot and it will spit — wait ten minutes, and leave the lid vented.

steps.text: Pour the purée over the mutton, add the tamarind extract, jaggery and salt, and simmer uncovered 20 minutes, stirring every few minutes.
steps.tip: It sticks readily once thick. Use a flat wooden spoon and scrape the base.

steps.text: Taste and balance — it should land sour first, then sweet, then hot. Add tamarind or jaggery a teaspoon at a time.
Fry the sliced onion in the remaining 2 tbsp oil until dark brown and crisp, about 10 minutes over medium heat.
Rest the dhansak 10 minutes off the heat, then top with the fried onion, mint and coriander leaves.

recipes.storage: Keeps 3 days refrigerated and freezes well for 2 months. It thickens overnight — loosen with hot water and reheat gently, as a fast reheat scorches the dal.

recipes.name: Jardaloo Ma Gosht
recipes.subtitle: mutton braised with dried apricots until the gravy turns sweet, sour and dark

ingredients.note: Hunza apricots with the stone in are the traditional choice
for colour without more heat
cane vinegar if you have it

ingredients.qty: 2 medium, cut into fine matchsticks and fried crisp
ingredients.note: the sali topping

prepNotes: Soak the apricots in 200ml warm water for 30 minutes. Keep the soaking water — it goes into the gravy.
Bring the mutton to room temperature and pat it dry, or it will steam rather than brown.
If you are making sali at home, soak the potato matchsticks in cold water 15 minutes, dry them thoroughly, then fry in batches.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a heavy pan and fry the cinnamon and cloves for 30 seconds, until the cloves swell.
Add the sliced onion and cook over medium heat until deep brown, 18-20 minutes, stirring so the edges do not catch.
steps.tip: This is where the colour of the dish comes from. Brown, never black — burnt onion turns the whole gravy bitter.

steps.text: Stir in the ginger and garlic paste and fry 2 minutes, until the raw smell goes.
Add turmeric, coriander, cumin, chilli powder and Kashmiri chilli. Fry 40 seconds with a splash of water so they do not scorch.
Add the mutton and brown it hard for 8 minutes, until the pieces are sealed and the oil separates at the edges.
Add the tomato and salt, cover, and cook 10 minutes until the tomato collapses into the masala.
Pour in the water, bring to a boil, then simmer covered 55-65 minutes until the mutton is tender. In a pressure cooker, 4 whistles then 10 minutes on low.
Add the soaked apricots with their water, the jaggery and the vinegar. Simmer uncovered 12 minutes.
steps.tip: Add the apricots this late or they dissolve. You want them whole and plump against the meat.

steps.text: Taste and balance: it should read sweet first, then sour, then hot. Adjust with a little more jaggery or vinegar.
steps.tip: Balancing is the whole recipe. Do it off the heat, a teaspoon at a time.

steps.text: Stir in the garam masala, rest 5 minutes off the heat, and pile the fried sali on top just before serving.
steps.tip: Sali goes on at the table. Sat in the gravy it goes soft in two minutes.

recipes.storage: Keeps 3 days refrigerated and tastes better on day two. Reheat gently with a splash of water; fry fresh sali rather than reheating old.

recipes.name: Kheema Par Eeda
recipes.subtitle: spiced mutton mince with eggs baked into the surface, soft yolks over dry kheema

ingredients.note: for cracking over the eggs

prepNotes: Use a wide pan with a lid — you need enough surface area to sit four eggs apart from each other.
Bring the eggs to room temperature so the whites set evenly on the hot kheema.
The kheema must be dry before the eggs go on. Wet mince makes the whites run together into a puddle.

steps.text: Heat the ghee in a wide kadhai and fry the onion until golden brown, 12 minutes.
Add ginger, garlic and green chilli and fry 2 minutes.
Add turmeric, chilli powder, coriander and cumin powder, and fry 30 seconds.
Add the mince and break it up with the back of a spoon, frying 8 minutes until it loses all pinkness and starts to catch.
steps.tip: Break the lumps early. Once the mince sets in clumps you will not get it smooth again.

steps.text: Add the tomato and salt and cook 6 minutes until the tomato disappears into the mince.
Add the water, cover, and simmer 12 minutes, then uncover and cook off every trace of liquid, about 5 minutes.
steps.tip: Dry means dry — tilt the pan and no gravy should run.

steps.text: Stir through the garam masala, coriander leaves and mint, then level the surface and press four shallow wells with the back of a spoon.
Crack an egg into each well, season with salt and the coarse black pepper.
Cover and cook on the lowest heat 8-10 minutes, until the whites are opaque and the yolks still wobble.
steps.tip: Check at 8 minutes. A minute too long and you lose the runny yolk that makes the dish.

steps.text: Bring the pan to the table and serve with pav or rotli.

recipes.storage: Best eaten straight away for the soft yolks. Leftover kheema alone keeps 2 days refrigerated; reheat and crack fresh eggs onto it.

recipes.name: Kolmi no Patio
recipes.subtitle: prawns in a thick red tamarind masala that is fiery, sour and sweet at once

ingredients.note: for colour

prepNotes: Soak the dried red chillies in hot water for 20 minutes before grinding, or the masala will stay gritty.
Toss the prawns with 1/2 tsp turmeric and 1 tsp salt and leave 15 minutes, then rinse and pat dry.
Squeeze the tamarind and strain out the fibres and seeds before you begin cooking.

steps.text: Grind the soaked chillies, garlic, ginger, cumin seeds, kashmiri chilli and 2 tbsp of the soaking water to a smooth red paste.
steps.tip: Grind it properly smooth — patio should be a paste-thick masala, not a chunky curry.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a kadhai and fry the curry leaves for 20 seconds until they crackle and go translucent.
Add the onion and cook 10 minutes over medium heat until soft and pale gold.
Add the ground masala and fry 6 to 8 minutes, stirring constantly, until the oil pools around the edges and the raw garlic smell disappears.
steps.tip: This is the whole dish. Under-fried masala tastes harsh no matter how much jaggery you add later.

steps.text: Stir in the turmeric, coriander powder and tomato and cook 6 minutes until the tomato has collapsed completely.
Add the tamarind extract, jaggery, vinegar and salt and simmer 5 minutes to a thick, glossy masala.
Taste and balance the three points — sour, sweet, hot. It should be assertive on all three, since the prawns will mute it.
Slide in the prawns, stir to coat, and cook 3 to 4 minutes only, until they curl and turn opaque.
steps.tip: Prawns go rubbery the moment they overcook. Take the pan off the heat while they still look barely done.

steps.text: Rest 5 minutes off the heat, scatter with coriander leaves, and serve with plain rice or rotli.

recipes.storage: Keeps 2 days refrigerated. Reheat only until warm through — a second full simmer will toughen the prawns. The masala base alone freezes 2 months.

recipes.name: Lagan nu Custard
recipes.subtitle: the dense baked wedding custard, caramel-topped and heavy with nutmeg and cardamom
prepNotes: Reduce the milk well ahead — this is the step that takes the time, and rushing it gives a loose, watery custard.
Bring the eggs to room temperature so they blend into the warm milk without scrambling.
Preheat the oven to 160C a full 20 minutes before baking, and set a tray of hot water on the lower shelf.

steps.text: Boil the milk in a wide heavy pan and simmer 30 minutes, stirring often, until reduced to about 600ml.
steps.tip: Scrape the sides back in as it reduces — those caramelised scrapings are where the flavour lives.

steps.text: Stir in the condensed milk and sugar and simmer 5 minutes more, then take off the heat and cool to lukewarm.
Beat the eggs until just smooth, with no strands of white remaining.
Pour a ladle of the warm milk into the eggs while whisking, then repeat twice before adding the eggs back into the pan.
steps.tip: Tempering is not optional. Tip cold eggs into hot milk and you get sweet scrambled egg.

steps.text: Whisk in the ground cardamom, nutmeg and rose water.
Strain the mixture through a fine sieve into a ghee-rubbed baking dish about 25cm across.
steps.tip: Straining catches the inevitable few threads of cooked egg and is what makes the texture silky.

steps.text: Scatter the slivered almonds and pistachios over the surface.
Bake at 160C for 45 to 55 minutes, until the edges are set and the centre wobbles like a soft jelly when nudged.
steps.tip: A cracked, puffed surface means it went too far. Pull it while the middle still moves.

steps.text: If the top has not browned, run it under a hot grill for 2 minutes until patched with dark caramel spots.
Cool completely at room temperature, at least 3 hours, before cutting into squares.

recipes.storage: Refrigerate up to 4 days, covered. Serve chilled or at room temperature — it is never reheated, and it firms up and tastes better on the second day.

recipes.name: Machhi No Saas
recipes.subtitle: pomfret poached in a pale sweet-sour sauce thickened with egg and rice flour

ingredients.qty: 600g pomfret or seer, cut into 4 steaks

ingredients.note: the traditional thickener
cane vinegar

prepNotes: Rub the fish steaks with salt and a squeeze of the vinegar and leave 20 minutes, then rinse and pat dry.
Grind the garlic, green chilli, cumin seeds and ginger to a fine paste with 2 tbsp water before you start cooking.
Slake the rice flour in 4 tbsp cold water and keep it beside the stove — added dry it will lump instantly.

steps.text: Heat the oil and cook the onion gently until soft and translucent but not coloured, 8 minutes.
steps.tip: Saas is a pale sauce. Brown onion here and it will look and taste wrong.

steps.text: Add the ground garlic-chilli-cumin paste and fry 2 minutes, until it stops smelling raw.
Pour in the water with salt, bring to a simmer, and cook 5 minutes.
Stir in the slaked rice flour and simmer 4 minutes, stirring, until the sauce coats a spoon lightly.
Slide in the fish steaks in a single layer and poach on low 8-10 minutes, spooning sauce over rather than turning them.
steps.tip: Turning breaks the steaks. Baste instead.

steps.text: Lift the fish out onto a serving dish and keep it warm.
Beat the eggs with the vinegar until smooth.
Take the pan off the heat, wait a minute, then trickle in the egg-vinegar mixture in a thin stream while whisking hard.
steps.tip: Off the heat and slowly. Straight into a boiling pan the egg scrambles and the sauce is ruined.

steps.text: Return to the lowest heat with the sugar and stir 2 minutes until the sauce thickens to a thin custard. It must not boil.
Taste for the sweet-sour balance, pour over the fish, scatter with coriander and serve with plain boiled rice.

recipes.storage: Eat the same day. Refrigerated it keeps 1 day; reheat over the gentlest heat or in a bain-marie, as a boil will split the egg-thickened sauce.

recipes.name: Margi Na Farcha
recipes.subtitle: chicken marinated overnight, dipped in beaten egg and fried crisp for wedding lunches

ingredients.qty: 800g, 8 bone-in thigh and drumstick pieces, skin off

ingredients.note: into the egg batter

prepNotes: Slash each piece of chicken to the bone twice and marinate overnight, or at least 4 hours, refrigerated.
Take the chicken out of the fridge 30 minutes before frying so it cooks through evenly.
Beat the eggs only when the chicken is cooked and cooling — batter beaten too early goes flat.

steps.text: Mix the ginger and garlic paste, all the ground spices, the vinegar, lemon juice and salt into a thick marinade.
Rub it hard into the slashed chicken, working it into the cuts, and refrigerate overnight.
steps.tip: The cuts matter — without them the marinade sits on the surface and the meat inside tastes of nothing.

steps.text: Tip the chicken with all its marinade into a wide pan, add the water, cover, and cook over medium heat 18-20 minutes, turning once.
Uncover and cook off the liquid until the pieces are coated in a thick, almost dry masala. Cool completely on a plate.
steps.tip: The chicken must be cool and dry, or the egg coating slides off in the oil.

steps.text: Beat the eggs with a pinch of salt and the chopped coriander until pale and frothy.
Heat the oil in a kadhai to 175C — a drop of batter should rise and sizzle in 3 seconds.
Dip a chicken piece in the egg, let the excess drip for two seconds, and lower it into the oil away from you.
Fry 2-3 pieces at a time for 3-4 minutes, spooning egg over any bald patches, until the coating is golden and puffed.
steps.tip: Crowding drops the oil temperature and the coating turns greasy instead of crisp.

steps.text: Drain on a rack, not paper, so the underside stays crisp.
Serve hot with lemon wedges and a plate of rotli, or alongside pulao dal.

recipes.storage: Best within an hour of frying. The cooked, unfried masala chicken keeps 2 days refrigerated — bring it to room temperature and egg-fry to order.

recipes.name: Mutton Pulao Dal
recipes.subtitle: brown-rice mutton pulao served with a smooth toor dal, the Sunday lunch of Parsi homes

ingredients.note: caramelised, for the brown colour of the rice
for the dal

prepNotes: Soak the rice 30 minutes and drain it in a colander for 15 more, so the grains are damp but not wet.
Make the caramel first and have it cool in a cup: 2 tbsp sugar melted in a dry pan to a dark mahogany, killed with 2 tbsp hot water.
The dal and the pulao cook in parallel. Start the dal first — it can sit while the rice steams.
Take the mutton out of the fridge 30 minutes ahead.

steps.text: For the dal, pressure cook the toor dal with the tomato, turmeric, half the chilli powder, salt and 700ml water for 5 whistles, then blend smooth and keep warm.
steps.tip: Blend it properly. Parsi dal is silk, not a textured tadka dal.

steps.text: Heat 2 tbsp ghee, crackle the cumin seeds, add 1 sliced onion and fry to deep gold, then pour this over the dal.
For the pulao, heat 4 tbsp ghee in a heavy pot and fry the remaining sliced onion until dark brown, 20 minutes. Lift out half and reserve for the top.
steps.tip: Twenty minutes on medium, not ten on high. Rushed onion is bitter and pale in the same breath.

steps.text: Add cinnamon, cloves, cardamom, black cardamom, bay leaves and peppercorns to the pot and fry 1 minute.
Add the ginger and garlic paste, fry 2 minutes, then add the mutton and brown it 8 minutes.
Add the rest of the chilli powder, salt and 700ml water. Pressure cook 4 whistles, or simmer covered 60 minutes, until the mutton is tender.
Strain the meat from the stock. Measure the stock and make it up with water to 900ml — this is what the rice will drink.
steps.tip: Getting the liquid right is the difference between separate grains and porridge.

steps.text: Bring the stock to a boil with the caramel, the garam masala and salt. It should taste slightly too salty on its own.
Stir in the drained rice and the mutton, boil hard 4 minutes until craters appear on the surface, then cover tightly and cook on the lowest heat 15 minutes.
Rest, still covered, for 10 minutes off the heat before opening.
steps.tip: Do not lift the lid early. The last of the steam is what finishes the top layer of rice.

steps.text: Fork the rice through gently, scatter the reserved brown onion and coriander over, and serve with the hot dal in a bowl alongside.

recipes.storage: Rice and dal both keep 2 days refrigerated, stored separately. Reheat the rice covered with a sprinkle of water; loosen the dal with water and bring it back to a bare simmer.

recipes.name: Papeta Ma Gosht
recipes.subtitle: everyday mutton and potato stew, gently spiced and thickened by the potatoes themselves
prepNotes: Cut the potatoes big — quarters, not chunks — or they will disintegrate before the mutton is done.
Keep the peeled potatoes in cold water until they go into the pan so they do not grey.
Take the mutton out of the fridge 30 minutes ahead.

steps.text: Heat the oil and fry the chopped onion over medium heat until soft and pale gold, about 10 minutes.
steps.tip: This is a gentler dish than jardaloo ma gosht. Do not brown the onion hard.

steps.text: Add ginger and garlic paste with the slit green chillies and fry 2 minutes.
Add turmeric, chilli powder, coriander and cumin powder. Fry 30 seconds.
Add the mutton and brown 6 minutes, turning the pieces so each face colours.
Add the tomato and salt and cook 8 minutes until the tomato has broken down and the oil rises.
Pour in the water and simmer covered 45 minutes, or pressure cook 3 whistles and release naturally.
Add the potatoes, cover, and cook 20 minutes more until a knife slides through them with no resistance.
steps.tip: Crush two potato pieces against the side of the pan — that is what thickens the gravy.

steps.text: Stir in the garam masala and simmer uncovered 5 minutes to reduce to a pouring consistency.
Finish with coriander leaves and the lemon juice, and rest 5 minutes before serving with rotli or plain rice.

recipes.storage: Keeps 3 days refrigerated. Reheat over low heat with a little water; the potatoes soak up gravy overnight, so expect to loosen it.

recipes.name: Papeta par Eeda
recipes.subtitle: eggs baked on a bed of soft spiced potatoes, the everyday parsi supper

ingredients.qty: 500g, peeled and cut into thin matchsticks

ingredients.note: neutral oil works, but ghee is the traditional fat

prepNotes: Cut the potato into fine even matchsticks — thick pieces stay hard while the eggs overcook waiting for them.
Rinse the cut potato and dry it well so it fries rather than steams.
Use a wide pan you can cover, so all the eggs sit in a single layer on the potato.

steps.text: Heat the ghee in a wide kadhai and fry the sliced onion 6 minutes until soft and lightly golden.
Add the green chilli and cook 1 minute.
Stir in the turmeric, cumin powder and chilli powder and fry 30 seconds.
Add the potato matchsticks with 1 tsp salt and toss until every strand is coated yellow.
Sprinkle over 3 tbsp water, cover, and cook 12 to 14 minutes on low, shaking the pan every few minutes.
steps.tip: Shake rather than stir. Stirring breaks the potato into mash.

steps.text: Uncover and check — a matchstick should give completely under a spoon but the mass should still be loose, not sticky.
Fold in half the coriander leaves, then flatten the potato into an even bed and make five shallow wells with the back of a spoon.
Crack one egg into each well, season with salt and black pepper, cover, and cook on the lowest heat 6 to 8 minutes.
steps.tip: Cover it — the steam is what sets the tops. Lift the lid at 6 minutes and check; the whites should be opaque and the yolks still liquid.

steps.text: Scatter the remaining coriander over and bring the pan straight to the table with pav or rotli.

recipes.storage: Best eaten straight from the pan. Leftover potato base keeps 2 days refrigerated and reheats well in a covered pan — cook fresh eggs on it rather than reheating set ones.

recipes.name: Patra ni Machhi
recipes.subtitle: pomfret packed in green coconut chutney and steamed in a leaf until it flakes

ingredients.qty: 4 pomfret fillets, about 150g each, or 2 small whole pomfret
ingredients.note: any firm white fish works
frozen grated coconut, thawed, is fine
balances the lime
cane vinegar if you have it

prepNotes: Pat the fish bone dry, rub with half the lemon juice and 1/2 tsp salt, and rest 15 minutes in the fridge.
Soften banana leaves over a low flame for a few seconds until they turn glossy and pliable — they crack if used cold. Baking parchment works if you cannot find them.
Grate the coconut fresh if you can; desiccated coconut makes a dry, grainy chutney.

steps.text: Blend the coconut, coriander, mint, green chilli, garlic, cumin seeds, sugar, turmeric, remaining lemon juice, vinegar and salt to a thick paste.
steps.tip: Add water a tablespoon at a time, no more than 3 tbsp total. A watery chutney runs off the fish.

steps.text: Taste the chutney and correct it now — it should be sharp, sweet and hot all at once, and it will taste milder once steamed.
Cut the softened banana leaf into rectangles roughly twice the size of each fillet.
Spread a spoon of chutney on the leaf, lay the fish on it, then blanket the fish with a thick layer of chutney on top and sides.
steps.tip: Be generous. The chutney is the dish, not a seasoning.

steps.text: Fold the leaf over into a snug parcel and tie with kitchen string or secure with a toothpick.
Set the parcels in a steamer over rapidly boiling water, cover, and steam 12 minutes for fillets or 18 for whole fish.
Open one parcel at the edge and press the thickest part — the flesh should part into flakes with no translucent centre.
steps.tip: Overcooked pomfret turns cottony in about two minutes flat. Check early.

steps.text: Rest the parcels 3 minutes off the heat, then serve them closed so each person opens their own.

recipes.storage: Best eaten the day it is made. Refrigerate leftover parcels up to 2 days and re-steam 5 minutes; never microwave, which toughens the fish.

recipes.name: Ravo
recipes.subtitle: birthday-morning semolina pudding, soft and milky with cardamom and fried raisins

ingredients.note: the traditional enrichment; leave out for an egg-free ravo

prepNotes: Warm the milk in a separate pan and keep it hot — cold milk hitting hot semolina makes lumps that never disperse.
Bring the egg to room temperature and beat it smooth before you need it.
Measure everything out first; once the semolina is roasted the dish moves quickly.

steps.text: Heat 2 tbsp ghee in a heavy pan and fry the raisins for 30 seconds until they puff, then lift them out.
Fry the slivered almonds in the same ghee for 45 seconds until pale gold and set them aside with the raisins.
Add the remaining ghee and the semolina and roast over low heat for 6 to 8 minutes, stirring constantly, until it smells nutty and turns the colour of pale sand.
steps.tip: Low heat and constant stirring. Semolina scorches at the base without warning and the burnt note carries through the whole pudding.

steps.text: Pour in the hot milk in a thin stream, whisking hard the whole time.
steps.tip: Whisk, do not stir. This is the only moment lumps can form, and once they do they stay.

steps.text: Add the pinch of salt and simmer 6 to 8 minutes, stirring, until the semolina swells and the mixture coats the back of a spoon.
Stir in the sugar and cook 3 minutes more; it will loosen at first and then thicken again.
Take the pan off the heat, let it cool for 2 minutes, then whisk in the beaten egg quickly and return to very low heat for 2 minutes.
steps.tip: Off the boil, whisking fast — otherwise the egg sets into threads instead of enriching the pudding.

steps.text: Stir in the cardamom, nutmeg and rose water, and thin with a splash of hot milk if it has gone past pourable.
Spoon into bowls, top with the fried raisins and almonds, and serve warm.

recipes.storage: Keeps 2 days refrigerated. It sets firm when cold — reheat gently with 3 to 4 tbsp of milk and whisk it back to a soft, spoonable consistency.

recipes.name: Sali Boti
recipes.subtitle: mutton in a sweet-sour tomato gravy under a haystack of crisp potato straws

ingredients.note: for colour without heat
makes it jardaloo ma boti; leave out for plain sali boti

ingredients.qty: 4 tbsp, plus 500ml for frying the sali

prepNotes: Marinate the mutton with the ginger-garlic paste, turmeric, 1 tbsp vinegar and 1 tsp salt for at least 1 hour, or overnight in the fridge.
Soak the dried apricots in warm water for 30 minutes so they plump rather than draw moisture from the gravy.
Cut the potato straws and soak them in cold water at least 20 minutes to rinse off the starch.

steps.text: Pound the ginger and garlic to a smooth paste and use half for the marinade, keeping half for the pan.
Heat 4 tbsp oil and fry the sliced onion over medium heat for 15 minutes until evenly deep brown.
steps.tip: This is where the gravy gets its body and colour. Brown, not black — pull it off the moment it smells nutty.

steps.text: Add the reserved ginger-garlic paste and green chilli and fry 2 minutes.
Stir in the kashmiri chilli, chilli powder, coriander powder and cumin powder and fry 1 minute until the oil takes on colour.
Tip in the tomato purée and cook 12 minutes until the oil separates and pools at the edges.
steps.tip: Do not shortcut this — raw tomato makes the gravy taste thin and sharp.

steps.text: Add the marinated mutton and sear 6 minutes, stirring, until every cube is coated and no pink shows.
Pour in 400ml water, cover, and simmer 45 minutes, or pressure cook 4 whistles, until the mutton is tender.
Stir in the jaggery, remaining vinegar, garam masala, soaked apricots and salt and simmer uncovered 10 minutes.
steps.tip: The finish should be clearly sweet and clearly sour. Adjust jaggery and vinegar together, not one alone.

steps.text: Drain and dry the potato straws thoroughly, then fry in 500ml hot oil in two batches for 3 minutes each until pale gold and crisp.
steps.tip: Wet straws will spit and go limp. Blot them dry on a cloth first.

steps.text: Drain the sali on paper, salt lightly, and pile over the mutton just before serving.

recipes.storage: The gravy keeps 3 days refrigerated and improves on day two. Store the sali separately in an airtight tin for up to a week and never refrigerate them, or they go soft.

recipes.name: Salli Marghi
recipes.subtitle: chicken in a tangy tomato-onion gravy crowned with matchstick potatoes

ingredients.note: for the salli

ingredients.qty: 3 tbsp, plus 500ml for frying the salli

prepNotes: Rub the chicken with 1/2 tsp turmeric, 1 tsp salt and 1 tbsp vinegar and leave 30 minutes at room temperature.
Soak the potato matchsticks in cold water 20 minutes, then drain and dry them completely on a cloth.
Pound the ginger and garlic together to a paste rather than using them separately.

steps.text: Heat 3 tbsp oil with the cinnamon and cloves until the spices swell, about 40 seconds.
Add the sliced onion and fry 12 minutes over medium heat to a deep even brown.
steps.tip: Salt the onion lightly at the start — it draws out water and browns faster.

steps.text: Add the ginger-garlic paste and green chilli and fry 2 minutes until the raw edge is gone.
Stir in the turmeric, kashmiri chilli, chilli powder, coriander powder and cumin powder and fry 45 seconds.
steps.tip: Add a splash of water if the pan looks dry; ground spices burn in seconds and turn the gravy bitter.

steps.text: Add the tomato and cook 10 minutes, mashing with the spoon, until it breaks down and the oil separates.
Add the marinated chicken and turn it in the masala over high heat for 5 minutes until it is sealed all over.
Pour in 300ml water, cover, and simmer 20 minutes until the chicken pulls easily from the bone.
Stir in the jaggery, remaining vinegar, garam masala and salt and simmer uncovered 5 minutes to a gravy that just coats a spoon.
Fry the dried potato matchsticks in 500ml hot oil in two batches, 3 minutes each, until pale gold, then drain and salt.
steps.tip: Pull them out a shade lighter than you want — they darken as they cool.

steps.text: Scatter the coriander leaves over the chicken and heap the salli on top at the table.

recipes.storage: The gravy keeps 3 days refrigerated; reheat with a splash of water. Keep the salli in an airtight tin at room temperature for up to a week and add them only at serving.

recipes.name: Sev
recipes.subtitle: vermicelli fried in ghee and sweetened with raisins, almonds and cardamom for birthday mornings

ingredients.note: wheat seviyan, not rice noodles
soaked in 1 tbsp warm water

prepNotes: Soak the raisins in warm water for 10 minutes so they plump rather than burn in the ghee.
Have the water measured and hot before you start roasting — cold water hitting hot vermicelli makes it clump.
Sev is eaten at Parsi birthdays and on Navroze morning, usually with dahi alongside.

steps.text: Melt the ghee over medium-low heat and fry the almonds and pistachios for 1 minute until they just colour. Lift them out.
Fry the drained raisins in the same ghee for 30 seconds, until they swell. Lift them out too.
steps.tip: They puff and then burn very quickly. Watch them, do not walk away.

steps.text: Add the broken vermicelli and roast, stirring constantly, 5-7 minutes until it is an even reddish brown and smells nutty.
steps.tip: Even colour is everything. Stir continuously and keep the heat moderate — the strands at the edge catch first.

steps.text: Pour in the hot water with the pinch of salt. It will hiss violently. Stir once.
Cover and cook on low 6 minutes, until the vermicelli is soft and almost all the water has gone.
Add the sugar and stir. The mixture will loosen again as the sugar melts.
steps.tip: The sugar goes in after the vermicelli is soft. Add it early and the strands stay hard.

steps.text: Cook uncovered 6-8 minutes, stirring gently, until the syrup has been absorbed and the sev is glossy and just moist.
Stir in the crushed cardamom, nutmeg, saffron water and rose water, then fold back the nuts and raisins.
Rest covered 5 minutes off the heat and serve warm, with plain yogurt on the side.

recipes.storage: Keeps 3 days refrigerated. Reheat in a pan with a tablespoon of milk or water and a knob of ghee to bring the gloss back; microwaving dries it out.

recipes.name: Tamota Par Eeda
recipes.subtitle: eggs set over sweet-sour stewed tomatoes, a fifteen-minute Parsi supper

ingredients.note: to lift the tomatoes

prepNotes: Use ripe, soft tomatoes — this dish is almost entirely tomato, so hard winter ones will taste thin.
Have the eggs at room temperature and crack each into a small cup first, so a broken yolk never lands in the pan.
Pick a pan just wide enough for four eggs to sit apart, around 24cm.

steps.text: Heat the ghee and fry the onion over medium heat until soft and just golden, 8 minutes.
Add the garlic, ginger and green chilli and fry 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in turmeric, chilli powder and cumin powder for 20 seconds.
Add the tomato, sugar and salt. Cook uncovered 10-12 minutes, mashing occasionally, until the mixture is jammy and no watery liquid pools at the edge.
steps.tip: If it is still wet the eggs will slide around and never set properly.

steps.text: Stir in half the coriander leaves and level the surface.
Make four wells and slip in the eggs, then season them with salt and the black pepper.
Cover and cook on the lowest heat 6-8 minutes, until the whites are just set and the yolks are still soft.
steps.tip: Lowest heat, lid on. The steam sets the tops of the whites without hardening the yolks.

steps.text: Scatter the remaining coriander over and serve straight from the pan with buttered pav or rotli.

recipes.storage: Eat immediately — the yolks are the point and do not survive reheating. The tomato base alone keeps 2 days refrigerated.

recipes.name: Aloo Gobi
recipes.subtitle: dry-cooked potato and cauliflower, browned at the edges and heavy on ginger

image.alt: Aloo gobi, potato and cauliflower with tomato and coriander

ingredients.qty: 1 medium (700g), cut into small florets with a little stalk on each
3 medium (400g), peeled and cut into 2cm cubes
2 inch, half grated and half julienned
ingredients.note: aloo gobi wants more ginger than you think

ingredients.qty: 4 tbsp, heated to smoking and cooled
ingredients.note: or neutral oil

prepNotes: Cut the florets small and dry them thoroughly on a cloth after washing. Wet cauliflower steams and goes limp instead of browning.
Keep the potato cubes the same size as the florets so they finish together.
Have a lid ready — the vegetables cook covered on low, in their own steam, with no added water.

steps.text: Heat 3 tbsp of the oil in a wide kadhai until it shimmers and crackle the cumin seeds for 20 seconds.
Fry the potato cubes on medium-high for 6 minutes, undisturbed for the first 3, until they are gold on several faces, then lift them out.
steps.tip: Moving them too early tears the crust off. Let them sit.

steps.text: Add the cauliflower to the same pan with the remaining oil and fry 6 minutes until browned in patches.
steps.tip: Brown patches on the florets are the flavour of this dish. Do not crowd the pan.

steps.text: Push the cauliflower aside, add the onion, and fry 5 minutes until soft and gold.
Stir in the grated ginger, garlic and green chillies and fry 90 seconds.
Add the turmeric, coriander powder and chilli powder, stir 20 seconds, then add the tomato and 1 tsp salt.
Cook 6 minutes until the tomato has broken down into a coating masala rather than a gravy.
Return the potatoes, stir to coat everything, cover and cook on the lowest heat for 10 minutes, shaking the pan every few minutes.
steps.tip: No water. The vegetables release enough of their own and water turns this into a mush.

steps.text: Check that a knife slides into both potato and stalk with no resistance; give it 5 minutes more if not.
Uncover, stir in the amchur and garam masala, and cook 2 minutes to dry it off.
Finish with the julienned ginger and coriander and serve with roti.

recipes.storage: Keeps 3 days refrigerated. Reheat in a dry pan on medium so it crisps again rather than steaming. Does not freeze — the cauliflower collapses.

recipes.name: Aloo Methi
recipes.subtitle: cubed potato and fresh fenugreek fried dry, bitter and sweet in the same mouthful

ingredients.note: about two large bunches, stems discarded
or mustard oil for a sharper version

prepNotes: Pick the methi leaves off the stems, wash in three changes of water and drain thoroughly. Wet leaves steam the potatoes.
Sprinkle the picked leaves with 1/2 tsp salt, rest 15 minutes and squeeze out the dark liquid if you want the bitterness tamed. Skip it if you like it bitter.
Cut the potato cubes evenly so they finish at the same time — this dish is not covered or stirred much.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a kadhai and crackle the cumin seeds for 15 seconds.
Add the sliced garlic and fry 40 seconds until it just turns pale gold.
steps.tip: Garlic browns in seconds here. Pull it back the moment it colours or it will taste burnt through the whole dish.

steps.text: Add the onion and green chilli and fry 4 minutes until soft and translucent.
Tip in the potato cubes, turmeric and salt and toss to coat. Spread them into a single layer.
Fry uncovered on medium for 10-12 minutes, turning only every 3 minutes, until the cubes are browned on several faces and nearly tender.
steps.tip: Stirring constantly breaks the potato into mash. Leave it alone between turns.

steps.text: Add the chilli powder and coriander powder and toss for 1 minute.
Add the methi leaves in handfuls, letting each batch wilt before the next goes in. This takes about 3 minutes.
Raise the heat and stir-fry 5 minutes more until the leaves have darkened and the pan is dry, with no green liquid pooling.
steps.tip: Fresh methi throws a lot of water. Cook it all off or the dish tastes washed out.

steps.text: Sprinkle over the amchur, toss once and take off the heat. Serve hot with phulka.

recipes.storage: Keeps 2 days refrigerated. Reheat dry in a hot pan for 3-4 minutes; adding water turns it soggy. It does not freeze well.

recipes.name: Aloo Paratha
recipes.subtitle: wholewheat flatbread stuffed with spiced potato and griddled in ghee

ingredients.note: optional in many households

ingredients.qty: 6 tbsp, for the dough and the tawa

prepNotes: Boil the potatoes the night before, or at least cool them completely. Warm potato releases steam inside the paratha and tears it open.
Knead the dough and rest it 30 minutes under a damp cloth — rested dough stretches around the filling instead of splitting.
Mash the potato dry with a fork or ricer. Never use a blender, which turns it to glue.

steps.text: Mix the atta with 1/2 tsp salt and 1 tbsp ghee, then add the water gradually and knead 8 minutes to a soft, smooth dough.
steps.tip: It should be softer than you think — barely holding its shape. Stiff dough makes hard parathas.

steps.text: Cover with a damp cloth and rest 30 minutes.
Mash the cold potatoes and mix in the onion, green chilli, ginger, coriander, amchur, crushed cumin, chilli powder, garam masala, ajwain and 1 tsp salt.
Taste the filling and correct the salt and sour — it should taste slightly over-seasoned on its own.
Divide dough and filling into 8 each, and roll both into balls.
Flatten a dough ball into a 4-inch disc, cup it in your palm, place a filling ball in the middle, and gather the edges over the top, pinching them shut.
steps.tip: Pinch off and discard the little knot of excess dough at the top, or that spot stays raw.

steps.text: Press the sealed ball flat, dust with flour, and roll gently to a 7-inch disc, working from the centre outward and turning as you go.
steps.tip: Even pressure. Lean on one spot and the filling bursts through.

steps.text: Lay it on a hot tawa and cook 60 seconds until the surface bubbles and the underside has pale spots.
Flip, brush the cooked side with ghee, and cook 60 seconds.
Flip once more, brush again, and press the edges down with a cloth until both sides are freckled deep brown, about 45 seconds.
Stack in a covered dish and serve hot with butter, yogurt and pickle.

recipes.storage: Best hot off the tawa. Keeps 1 day wrapped in foil in the fridge; reheat on a dry tawa 2 minutes a side. Uncooked stuffed parathas freeze 1 month between sheets of paper — cook from frozen on low heat.

recipes.name: Amritsari Fish
recipes.subtitle: ajwain-spiked gram flour batter fried crisp around soft white fish

ingredients.qty: 600g firm white fillets, cut into 5cm pieces
ingredients.note: sole, tilapia or river fish; pat very dry
for extra crispness
the signature flavour — do not leave it out

ingredients.qty: 1, half juiced and half cut into wedges

prepNotes: Pat the fish completely dry with kitchen paper and leave it uncovered in the fridge for 20 minutes. Wet fish sheds its batter in the oil.
Marinate the fish for 30 minutes, no longer — the lemon juice starts to break down the flesh after that.
Have a wire rack ready. Draining fried fish on paper steams the underside soft.

steps.text: Rub the fish pieces with the lemon juice, 1/2 tsp salt and the turmeric, and set aside 10 minutes.
Whisk the besan, rice flour, ginger, garlic, crushed ajwain, kashmiri chilli, black pepper and remaining salt in a bowl.
Add the water a tablespoon at a time until you have a batter the thickness of double cream.
steps.tip: It should coat a piece of fish and cling, not run off in sheets. Too thin is the most common mistake.

steps.text: Fold the fish through the batter, cover, and rest 30 minutes in the fridge.
Heat the oil in a kadhai to 170C — a drop of batter should sink briefly, then rise and sizzle steadily.
steps.tip: Too hot and the batter browns before the fish cooks; too cool and it drinks oil.

steps.text: Lower in 4 or 5 pieces at a time, without crowding, and fry 4 minutes until pale gold.
Lift onto the rack and let all the fish rest 5 minutes.
Raise the oil to 190C and fry the pieces a second time for 60 to 90 seconds until deep gold and crackling.
steps.tip: The double fry is what gives the shatter-crisp crust. Do not skip it.

steps.text: Drain on the rack, dust with chaat masala, and serve at once with lemon wedges and sliced onion.

recipes.storage: Best within the hour. Leftovers keep 1 day refrigerated; recrisp in a 200C oven for 8 minutes, never a microwave. The batter does not freeze.

recipes.name: Amritsari Kulcha
recipes.subtitle: crisp-bottomed stuffed maida bread, blistered and crushed under a spoonful of butter

ingredients.note: the stuffing must be cold and dry
for the top
generous, and non-negotiable

prepNotes: Boil the potatoes the day before if you can. Warm, freshly boiled potato steams inside the kulcha and tears it open.
The dough needs 2 hours at room temperature after kneading. Softer than chapati dough, almost sticky.
Get the oven and a heavy baking tray or upturned tawa to their maximum heat for at least 20 minutes before the first kulcha goes in.

steps.text: Mix the maida, baking soda, sugar and salt. Rub in the ghee, then work in the yogurt and enough lukewarm water to make a soft, slightly tacky dough. Knead 8 minutes until smooth.
Oil the surface of the dough, cover with a damp cloth and rest 2 hours in a warm spot. It should feel puffy and slack, not springy.
steps.tip: Under-rested dough gives you a hard flatbread rather than a kulcha.

steps.text: Grate the cold potatoes coarsely — do not mash. Mix with the onion, green chilli, ginger, coriander leaves, anardana, amchur, chaat masala, coriander powder, crushed cumin, chilli powder and salt.
steps.tip: Grated potato keeps the filling loose. Mashed potato turns to glue and pushes through the dough.

steps.text: Divide the dough and the filling into 6 each. Flatten a dough ball in your palm, cup a portion of filling inside, gather the edges over it and pinch shut. Rest the sealed balls 10 minutes, seam down.
Roll each ball out to a 15cm oval, using dry maida, pressing outwards from the centre with even weight and stopping if the filling threatens to break through.
Press nigella seeds and a little chopped coriander into the top surface, then flip and wet the underside with water using your palm.
Slap the wet side onto the screaming-hot tray or upturned tawa. It will stick. Bake or cook 3-4 minutes until the top blisters and browns in patches.
steps.tip: The water is what makes it grip the surface, exactly like a tandoor wall — do not skip it.

steps.text: If using a tawa, invert the tawa over the flame for 40 seconds to char the top directly.
Prise the kulcha off with a spatula, brush hard with softened butter, then crush it once between both palms so it cracks open.
steps.tip: The crush is the point — it shatters the crust and lets the butter into the filling.

steps.text: Serve immediately with pindi chole and sliced onion.

recipes.storage: Kulcha is a same-hour bread. It keeps 1 day wrapped in foil; revive on a hot tawa for 90 seconds a side with a smear of butter. The stuffing keeps 2 days refrigerated on its own.

recipes.name: Atte Ka Halwa
recipes.subtitle: wholewheat flour roasted in ghee until nutty, then swelled with hot sugar syrup

ingredients.note: equal weight to the flour; this is not the place to economise
replacing part of the water gives a softer halwa

ingredients.qty: a pinch, soaked in 1 tbsp warm milk

prepNotes: Measure the flour, ghee and sugar by equal weight and have the syrup already hot before you start roasting. Halwa gives you no time to improvise mid-way.
Bring the water and sugar to a boil in a separate pan and keep it simmering — cold syrup hitting hot flour makes lumps and spits violently.
Use a heavy kadhai. A thin pan scorches the flour in the last five minutes when it needs the most attention.

steps.text: Boil the water, milk and sugar together in a saucepan until the sugar dissolves, then keep it on the lowest heat.
Melt the ghee in a heavy kadhai over low-medium heat and add the atta all at once.
Stir constantly for 15-18 minutes. The mixture goes from pale and pasty, to loose and sandy, to a deep reddish-brown that smells like biscuits.
steps.tip: There is no shortcut. Under-roasted atta tastes floury and raw no matter how much ghee or sugar you add later.

steps.text: Watch for the ghee to separate and pool around the edges of the mass — that is the signal the flour is done.
Add the almonds and raisins and stir 1 minute so they toast in the ghee.
Take the kadhai off the flame, stand back, and pour in the hot syrup in three additions, stirring hard between each.
steps.tip: It will hiss and erupt. Off the flame and in stages is the only safe way to do this.

steps.text: Return to low heat and stir until the halwa thickens and pulls away from the sides of the pan, about 5 minutes.
Stir in the crushed cardamom and the saffron milk, cover and rest 5 minutes off the heat.
Serve warm, spooned into bowls, with the surface ghee left glistening on top.

recipes.storage: Keeps 4 days refrigerated in a covered box. It sets firm when cold; reheat in a pan on low with 2 tbsp milk, stirring until it loosens. Do not microwave, which makes it rubbery.

recipes.name: Baingan Bharta
recipes.subtitle: fire-roasted aubergine mashed rough with onion and tomato, smoky throughout

image.alt: Baingan bharta, smoked mashed aubergine with spring onion

ingredients.qty: 2 large (900g total), the fat round purple kind
6 cloves, minced, plus 4 whole cloves for roasting
3 tbsp, heated to smoking and cooled
ingredients.note: or neutral oil

prepNotes: Choose aubergines that feel light for their size — those have fewer seeds and roast sweeter.
Make four small slits in each aubergine and push a whole garlic clove into each, then rub the skin with oil.
Roast directly over a gas flame if you can. The smoke is the point of the dish and an oven cannot fully replace it.

steps.text: Set the aubergines directly on a medium gas flame and roast 15 to 20 minutes, turning every few minutes with tongs.
steps.tip: It is done when the skin is blistered black all over and the whole thing sags like a deflated balloon.

steps.text: If you have no gas flame, roast at 240C for 45 minutes, turning twice, then blacken briefly under the grill.
Put the roasted aubergines in a covered bowl for 10 minutes — the steam loosens the skin.
Peel off every scrap of charred skin, then chop and mash the flesh roughly with a fork.
steps.tip: Do not rinse the flesh under the tap. You will wash the smoke straight down the drain.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a kadhai and crackle the cumin seeds for 20 seconds.
Add the onion and fry on medium-high for 10 minutes until deep gold.
Stir in the ginger, minced garlic and green chillies and fry 2 minutes.
Add the tomato, turmeric, coriander powder, chilli powder and 1 tsp salt, and cook 10 minutes until the tomato disappears into a thick masala and oil separates.
Fold in the mashed aubergine and cook 8 minutes on medium, pressing and stirring, until the mixture pulls away from the sides of the pan.
steps.tip: Keep the texture uneven. Bharta should never be smooth.

steps.text: Stir in the garam masala and most of the coriander, taste for salt, and finish with the rest of the coriander.

recipes.storage: Keeps 3 days refrigerated and the smokiness holds up well. Reheat in a pan, not a microwave. Freezes 2 months.

recipes.name: Bharwa Karela
recipes.subtitle: bitter gourds stuffed with sharp onion masala and cooked down slow until the skins wrinkle

ingredients.note: the traditional fat here
half for the stuffing, half for the salting

ingredients.qty: 2 tsp for salting, plus to taste

prepNotes: Scrape, slit and salt the karela at least 1 hour before cooking, and 3 hours is better. This is the only step that actually removes bitterness.
Keep the scraped peel — fried into the stuffing it adds a good rough texture. Discard it if you want the mildest version.
Have kitchen string or toothpicks ready to tie the stuffed gourds shut.

steps.text: Scrape the ridged skin off each karela with a knife, reserving the scrapings. Slit each one lengthways down one side without cutting through, and scoop out the seeds.
Rub the gourds inside and out with 2 tsp salt and 1/2 tsp turmeric and leave in a colander for 1-3 hours. Squeeze out the brown liquid and rinse once.
steps.tip: Squeeze hard — that bitter brown water is exactly what you are trying to get rid of.

steps.text: Heat 3 tbsp mustard oil in a kadhai until it smokes, cool for 30 seconds, then crackle the mustard seeds and crushed fenugreek.
Add the onion and the reserved scrapings and fry 10-12 minutes on medium until golden and dry.
Stir in the fennel, coriander, cumin, remaining turmeric, chilli powder, amchur, garam masala, green chilli and salt. Fry 3 minutes until the mixture smells toasted and looks dry.
steps.tip: The stuffing must be dry. Wet stuffing leaks out and steams the gourds instead of frying them.

steps.text: Cool the masala, fold in the coriander leaves, then pack it firmly into each karela and tie shut with string.
Heat the remaining 2 tbsp oil in a wide pan and lay the gourds in a single layer.
Cook uncovered on low for 25-30 minutes, turning every 5 minutes, until the skins are wrinkled, blistered and dark in patches.
steps.tip: Low and slow, uncovered. Covering the pan makes them soggy and grey.

steps.text: Press one with a spoon — it should give completely. Rest 5 minutes, snip the strings and serve with dal and roti.

recipes.storage: Keeps 4 days refrigerated and tastes better on day two. Reheat dry in a pan on low for 5 minutes; do not microwave, which makes the skins rubbery.

recipes.name: Bhindi Masala
recipes.subtitle: sliced okra fried dry until it loses all its slime, then tossed with onion and amchur

ingredients.qty: 600g, wiped clean and cut into 2cm lengths

prepNotes: Wash the okra whole an hour ahead and dry every pod with a cloth. Any water on the knife or the pod is what makes it slimy.
Trim the caps and tips and slice only once the pods are bone dry.
Do not add salt until the okra has finished frying — salt draws out moisture and brings the slime straight back.

steps.text: Heat 4 tbsp of the oil in a wide kadhai until it shimmers.
Add the okra in a single layer and fry on medium-high for 10 minutes, stirring only every 2 or 3 minutes.
steps.tip: Constant stirring is what makes okra go ropy. Leave it alone and let it sear.

steps.text: Keep frying until the pieces are browned in patches and no thread follows the spoon, about 4 minutes more.
steps.tip: Lift a piece with the spoon. If nothing strings behind it, you are done.

steps.text: Lift the okra out onto a plate and set aside.
Add the last tablespoon of oil to the pan and crackle the cumin and crushed fennel for 20 seconds.
Add the onion and fry 7 minutes on medium-high until soft with brown edges.
Stir in the ginger, garlic and green chillies and fry 90 seconds.
Add the turmeric, coriander powder and chilli powder, stir 20 seconds, then add the tomato wedges and 1 tsp salt.
Cook 5 minutes, just until the tomato softens but still holds its shape.
Return the okra, fold everything together gently, and cook 3 minutes uncovered.
steps.tip: Fold, do not stir hard, or the okra breaks up.

steps.text: Stir in the amchur and garam masala, scatter the coriander, and serve immediately.

recipes.storage: Keeps 2 days refrigerated. Reheat in a dry pan on high; a microwave brings the sliminess back. Do not freeze.

recipes.name: Butter Chicken
recipes.subtitle: Murgh makhani: charred chicken in a tomato and cream gravy, mild and fenugreek-scented

image.alt: Butter chicken served with butter naan

ingredients.note: for colour without heat
dried fenugreek leaves — not the seeds; this is the flavour most people cannot place
omit for a nut-free version; the gravy is thinner

prepNotes: The dish depends on two things: char on the chicken, and a gravy cooked long enough to lose its raw tomato edge. Neither is optional.
Thigh stays juicy through the double cooking; breast will dry out.
Kasuri methi (dried fenugreek leaves) crushed in at the end is the flavour most people cannot place. If you have it, use it.

steps.text: Marinate the chicken with the yogurt, half the ginger and garlic, the Kashmiri chilli, 1 tsp garam masala, lemon juice and salt. Leave at least 30 minutes, ideally 4 hours refrigerated.

Grill, broil or pan-sear the chicken in a very hot pan until the edges char in places and it is just cooked. Do not cook it through to dryness; it finishes in the sauce. Set aside with any resting juices.
Simmer the tomatoes with the remaining ginger and garlic, the cardamom and a splash of water, covered, for 20 minutes until completely collapsed.
Blend the tomato mixture smooth with the soaked cashews if using, then pass it through a sieve. The sieve is what separates a silky makhani from a rustic curry.
steps.tip: Discard the skins and seeds left in the sieve.

steps.text: Return the puree to the pan with the butter and cook 10 minutes over medium-low heat, stirring, until it darkens and thickens and the butter shows at the edges.
Add the chicken with its juices, the cream, the sugar and the remaining garam masala. Simmer 5 minutes. Crush the kasuri methi between your palms and stir it through. Taste for salt and lemon.

recipes.storage: Keeps 3 days refrigerated. Freeze the gravy without the cream for up to 2 months and add cream on reheating; frozen cream sauces can split.

recipes.name: Chana Masala
recipes.subtitle: everyday chickpeas in a dark, sour-edged onion-tomato masala

image.alt: Chana masala served with roti and samosa

ingredients.note: or 3 tins, drained, which cuts the cooking to 20 minutes

ingredients.qty: 2 inch, half grated and half julienned

ingredients.note: for a faint smokiness
dried pomegranate seeds — the sour backbone
use compounded-free hing to keep this gluten-free

prepNotes: Soak the dried chickpeas overnight in plenty of water with 1/2 tsp salt — at least 10 hours.
Crush the anardana coarsely in a mortar just before using; pre-ground it loses its edge within days.
If using tinned chickpeas, rinse them well and start at the masala step, simmering 20 minutes with 1.5 cups water.

steps.text: Drain the soaked chickpeas and pressure cook with 5 cups fresh water, the black cardamom and 1 tsp salt for 20 minutes at full pressure.
steps.tip: A cooked chickpea should crush completely against the roof of your mouth. Firm chickpeas never soften once the tomato goes in.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a heavy pan, crackle the cumin seeds and bay leaf for 20 seconds, then add the asafoetida.
Add the onion and fry on medium for 14 minutes, stirring often, until uniformly dark brown.
steps.tip: Take this further than feels comfortable. The colour of the finished dish comes almost entirely from here.

steps.text: Stir in the garlic, grated ginger and green chillies and fry 2 minutes.
Add the coriander powder, cumin powder, turmeric and chilli powder and stir for 20 seconds.
Pour in the tomato puree and cook 12 minutes until the masala is thick, glossy and pulling away from the pan with oil at the edges.
Add the cooked chickpeas with 2 cups of their cooking liquid and simmer uncovered 20 minutes.
Mash a ladleful of chickpeas against the side of the pan and stir them back in to thicken the gravy.
steps.tip: This is the difference between chickpeas in soup and chickpeas in masala.

steps.text: Stir in the crushed anardana, amchur and garam masala, and simmer 5 minutes more.
Taste and push the sour and salt until it makes you sit up, then top with julienned ginger, coriander and lemon wedges.

recipes.storage: Keeps 4 days refrigerated and is noticeably better on day two. Reheat with a splash of water. Freezes 3 months.

recipes.name: Chole
recipes.subtitle: Punjabi chickpea curry, dark and tangy with pomegranate and dried mango

ingredients.note: or 3 tins, drained
the smoky note that makes chole taste like chole

prepNotes: The dark colour of restaurant chole comes from cooking the chickpeas with a black tea bag or a piece of dried amla. Neither is required, but if you want the colour, add a tea bag to the cooking water and remove it before draining.
If using tinned chickpeas, simmer them in the finished gravy for 15 minutes so they absorb it; they will otherwise taste separate from the sauce.

steps.text: Pressure cook the soaked chickpeas with salt and the black cardamom in fresh water for 5-6 whistles, until a chickpea crushes easily between finger and thumb. Reserve the cooking liquid.

Heat the oil in a heavy pan. Add the cumin seeds and bay leaf, and when the cumin sizzles, add the onion. Fry patiently over medium heat until genuinely brown, 10-12 minutes; this is most of the flavour.
Add the ginger and garlic and cook for a minute until the raw smell goes, then add the tomato puree, turmeric, chilli powder and coriander powder.
Cook the masala down until the oil separates and pools at the edges of the pan, 8-10 minutes. Do not rush this.
Add the drained chickpeas with a cup of the reserved cooking liquid. Simmer uncovered 15 minutes, mashing a few chickpeas against the side of the pan to thicken the gravy.
Stir in the garam masala, a good squeeze of lemon and the coriander leaves. Rest 10 minutes off the heat before serving; chole improves noticeably in that time.

recipes.storage: Better on the second day. Keeps 4 days refrigerated, freezes 2 months. Reheat gently with a splash of water.

recipes.name: Dahi Bhalla
recipes.subtitle: feather-light urad dal dumplings drowned in sweetened yogurt with tamarind and roasted cumin

ingredients.note: keeps the bhalle light
use compounded-free hing to keep this gluten-free
one pressed into each bhalla

ingredients.qty: 2 litres, warm, for soaking the fried bhalle

prepNotes: Soak both dals separately for 5 hours. Drain them very well — wet dal makes a slack batter that drinks oil.
Grind with as little water as you can get away with, then beat the batter by hand for 5 minutes. Air beaten in now is what makes the bhalle spongy.
The yogurt should be whisked and chilled at least an hour ahead. Sour yogurt ruins the dish; use it the day you buy it.
Assemble no more than 30 minutes before serving, or the bhalle collapse.

steps.text: Grind the drained dals to a thick, smooth paste with 3-4 tbsp water only. The batter should hold a peak on the spoon.

Beat the batter hard with your hand or a whisk for 5 minutes, adding the asafoetida, ginger, green chilli, baking soda and salt. Drop a teaspoonful into a bowl of water — it should float within seconds.
steps.tip: The float test is the only reliable check. If it sinks, beat for another 3 minutes.

steps.text: Heat the oil to 170C. Wet your palm, take a spoon of batter, press a raisin into the centre and slide it in. Fry 5-6 at a time.
Fry 4-5 minutes, turning, to an even pale gold — not brown. Drain on paper.
steps.tip: Deep brown bhalle stay hard in the middle. Pale gold is correct here.

steps.text: Drop the hot bhalle straight into 2 litres of warm salted water and leave them 20 minutes. They will swell and go soft.

Meanwhile soak the tamarind in 200ml hot water for 15 minutes, squeeze out the pulp, strain, and simmer with the jaggery, 1/2 tsp of the roasted cumin and a pinch of black salt for 8 minutes until it coats a spoon.
Whisk the yogurt with the sugar and 1/2 tsp salt until it is smooth and pourable, like thin cream. Chill.
Lift each bhalla out of the water and press it flat between your palms to squeeze out the water. Be firm but do not tear it.
steps.tip: Squeezing properly is what lets the yogurt in. A waterlogged bhalla tastes of nothing.

steps.text: Arrange the pressed bhalle in a shallow dish and pour the chilled yogurt over to cover. Rest 20 minutes in the fridge.
Drizzle with the tamarind chutney, then dust with the remaining roasted cumin, black salt, chilli powder and chaat masala.
Scatter coriander, mint and pomegranate over and serve cold.

recipes.storage: Best within 4 hours of assembly. Fried bhalle keep 3 days refrigerated in their soaking water, or 1 month frozen undressed; the tamarind chutney keeps 3 weeks in the fridge. Dress only at serving time.

recipes.name: Dal Makhani
recipes.subtitle: black urad simmered for hours until it turns silky and smoky-sweet with butter

ingredients.note: whole black urad, not the split kind
red kidney beans, for body

ingredients.qty: 5 cups for cooking, plus more to loosen
2 inch, half crushed and half cut into fine julienne

ingredients.note: for colour rather than heat
to finish

prepNotes: Soak the urad and rajma together in plenty of cold water overnight, at least 8 hours. They should swell to double.
Cube the butter and return it to the fridge — cold butter emulsifies into the dal instead of splitting out as an oil slick.
Puree the tomatoes fresh; tinned puree is sharper and will need a pinch of sugar.

steps.text: Drain the soaked beans, put them in the pressure cooker with 5 cups water, half the crushed ginger and 1 tsp salt, and cook 25 minutes at full pressure.
steps.tip: Undercooked urad will never go creamy later, so err on the side of longer.

steps.text: Release the pressure and check: a bean should collapse to paste when pressed against the pot with a spoon. If not, give it another 10 minutes.
Heat the oil in a heavy pan, add the garlic paste and remaining crushed ginger and fry 90 seconds until the raw smell lifts.
Add the tomato puree, both chillies and 1/2 tsp salt, and fry on medium until the mixture darkens and oil beads at the edges, about 12 minutes.
steps.tip: This is the bhuna stage and it decides the whole dish. Stop early and the dal tastes of raw tomato.

steps.text: Tip the cooked beans in with all their liquid and stir well to break some of them up against the side of the pan.
Simmer uncovered on the lowest heat for 45 minutes, stirring every 5 minutes and scraping the base.
steps.tip: It will catch and scorch if you wander off. Add a splash of hot water whenever it looks tight.

steps.text: Stir in half the butter, a cube at a time, letting each melt before the next goes in.
Add the cream, garam masala and crushed kasuri methi, and simmer 10 minutes more until the dal coats a spoon thickly.
Taste for salt, then rest off the heat for 10 minutes so it thickens and settles.
Serve topped with the remaining butter, the julienned ginger and the coriander.

recipes.storage: Keeps 4 days refrigerated and tastes better on day two. Reheat gently with a splash of milk or water, stirring — it thickens hard when cold. Freezes 2 months without the final cream.

recipes.name: Dal Tadka
recipes.subtitle: everyday yellow dal finished with a loud garlic and chilli tempering

image.alt: Dal tadka finished with cream and coriander, served with naan

ingredients.note: yellow split moong, for creaminess
use compounded-free hing to keep this gluten-free

prepNotes: Rinse both dals in three changes of water until it runs clear — the starch on the surface makes the dal gluey and foamy.
Soak 20 minutes while you chop; it cuts the cooking time by a third.
Have the tempering ingredients in a small bowl beside the stove. The tadka takes 60 seconds and burns in 10.

steps.text: Pressure cook the drained dals with 3.5 cups water, the turmeric, half the chopped tomato and 1/2 tsp salt for 8 minutes at full pressure.
Let the pressure drop naturally, then whisk the dal briskly for 30 seconds until it is smooth and pourable.
steps.tip: Whisking is what gives dal its body. Add hot water if it is thicker than double cream.

steps.text: Keep the dal on the lowest simmer while you make the tempering.
Heat the ghee in a small pan until it shimmers, then add the cumin seeds and let them crackle and darken, about 20 seconds.
Add the sliced garlic and fry 60 seconds until the slices are gold at the edges.
steps.tip: Pull it off a shade early — the residual heat takes it further.

steps.text: Add the onion and fry 5 minutes until soft and browning.
Add the ginger, green chillies, broken red chillies and asafoetida and fry 30 seconds.
Add the remaining tomato and cook 4 minutes until it slumps and the ghee separates.
Take the pan off the heat, stir in the kashmiri chilli, and immediately pour the whole thing over the dal.
steps.tip: Off the heat. Chilli powder in hot ghee goes bitter almost instantly.

steps.text: Stir once, add the garam masala, lemon juice and coriander, and taste for salt.
Cover and rest 5 minutes before serving with rice.

recipes.storage: Keeps 3 days refrigerated. It sets solid when cold — reheat with plenty of hot water and re-whisk, then correct the salt and lemon. Freezes 2 months.

recipes.name: Gajar ka Halwa
recipes.subtitle: grated winter carrots cooked down in milk and ghee until dark, dense and cardamom-scented

ingredients.note: red winter carrots if you can get them; they are sweeter and less watery
adjust to how sweet the carrots are
or 3 tbsp milk powder stirred into the mix

prepNotes: Grate the carrots on the coarse side of the box grater, not in a food processor — processed carrot turns to wet pulp and the halwa never dries out.
Use a wide heavy pan. A narrow pan means the milk takes twice as long to reduce.
Crush the cardamom seeds fresh in a mortar just before adding; pre-ground loses its scent fast.

steps.text: Fry the cashews, almonds and raisins in 1 tbsp of the ghee for 2 minutes until the nuts are gold and the raisins puff, then lift them out.
Add 2 tbsp ghee to the pan and fry the grated carrot on medium for 10 minutes until it darkens and smells sweet.
steps.tip: This step drives off raw water early and deepens the colour. Do not skip straight to the milk.

steps.text: Pour in the milk and bring to a boil, then drop to medium-low.
Simmer uncovered 40 to 45 minutes, stirring every 5 minutes and scraping the base and sides.
steps.tip: Scrape the caramelised ring off the sides back into the pan each time — that is where the flavour is.

steps.text: Keep going until the milk is almost entirely gone and the mass pulls together when you draw the spoon through it.
Add the sugar and stir — the mixture will go loose again as the sugar melts.
steps.tip: Sugar goes in only after the milk has reduced. Add it early and the carrots stop softening.

steps.text: Cook 10 minutes more on medium until that liquid has gone too.
Stir in the crumbled khoya and the remaining 2 tbsp ghee and cook 8 minutes until the halwa is glossy and leaves the sides of the pan.
Fold in the crushed cardamom and most of the fried nuts and raisins.
Take off the heat, rest 10 minutes, and serve warm topped with the pistachios and remaining nuts.

recipes.storage: Keeps 5 days refrigerated in an airtight box. Reheat portions in a pan with a teaspoon of ghee, or microwave 40 seconds. Freezes 2 months; thaw overnight in the fridge before reheating.

recipes.name: Ghar Da Chicken Curry
recipes.subtitle: the plain everyday punjabi chicken curry, onion-heavy and thin enough to eat with roti

ingredients.note: bone-in is what gives the gravy body
or ghee
for colour without heat

prepNotes: Marinate the chicken in the yogurt, half the ginger-garlic paste, the turmeric and 1 tsp salt for 30 minutes at room temperature.
Heat mustard oil until it stops smoking before you cook in it, otherwise the curry tastes raw and bitter.
Slice the onions thin and uniform. They are the body of this gravy — there is no cream or cashew here.

steps.text: Heat the mustard oil in a kadhai until it smokes, then take it off the flame for 30 seconds to settle.
steps.tip: Raw mustard oil is pungent and sharp. Smoking it once fixes that permanently.

steps.text: Return to medium heat, crackle the cumin, then add the bay, black cardamom, cinnamon and cloves for 20 seconds.
Add the sliced onion and a pinch of salt and fry 15-18 minutes to a deep brown, stirring every minute or so.
steps.tip: This is the longest step and the one people cut short. Go until the onion is jammy and genuinely brown, not gold.

steps.text: Add the remaining ginger-garlic paste and the green chillies and fry 2 minutes.
Add the kashmiri chilli, coriander and cumin powders with 2 tbsp water and cook 1 minute so they do not scorch.
Add the tomato puree and cook 10 minutes on medium, until the mixture pulls together into a mass and oil rims the edge.
Add the marinated chicken with all its yogurt and fry on high for 6-7 minutes, until the pieces are sealed and coated and the yogurt has tightened.
steps.tip: Keep stirring while the yogurt goes in or it will split into curds.

steps.text: Pour in 500ml hot water, bring to a boil, then cover and simmer on low for 20 minutes.
Uncover and simmer 6-8 minutes more until the gravy coats a spoon thinly and the chicken pulls from the bone.
Crush in the kasuri methi, add the garam masala, cover and rest 5 minutes. Finish with coriander leaves and serve with roti.

recipes.storage: Keeps 3 days refrigerated; the gravy thickens overnight, so loosen with hot water when reheating. Freezes 2 months, though the chicken softens.

recipes.name: Keema Matar
recipes.subtitle: minced mutton browned hard with peas, the sunday lunch of a punjabi kitchen

ingredients.note: goat mince with some fat; lean mince goes dry
or mustard oil
at the end

prepNotes: Take the mince out of the fridge 20 minutes before cooking so it browns instead of steaming.
Chop the onions fine and evenly. This masala is bhuna-ed hard and uneven pieces burn before the rest colours.
If using frozen peas, thaw and drain them; add them only in the last 8 minutes or they turn grey.

steps.text: Heat the ghee in a pressure cooker, crackle the cumin, then add the bay, black cardamom, cinnamon and cloves for 20 seconds.
Add the onion and cook on medium for 12-14 minutes to a deep even gold, stirring often.
steps.tip: This is where the colour of the finished keema comes from. Pale onion, pale keema.

steps.text: Stir in the ginger and garlic pastes and the green chillies and fry 2 minutes, until the raw smell goes.
Add the turmeric, chilli powder, coriander and cumin powders with a splash of water and cook 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes and salt and cook 8-10 minutes until they collapse and the ghee separates at the edge of the pan.
Turn the heat high, add the mince and break it up constantly for 8 minutes until no pink remains and the grains are separate and browned.
steps.tip: Do not add water or cover it here. The mince must fry, not stew, or the keema tastes flat.

steps.text: Lower the heat, beat in the whisked yogurt a spoon at a time, and fry 3 minutes more.
Add 250ml water, close the cooker and cook 3 whistles, then 10 minutes on low. Rest until the pressure drops.
Open, stir in the peas and simmer uncovered 8 minutes, until the peas are tender and the keema is moist but not soupy.
steps.tip: Cook off any loose liquid at this stage — keema matar should hold its shape on a spoon.

steps.text: Crush in the kasuri methi, add the garam masala, cover and rest 5 minutes off the heat. Finish with coriander leaves.

recipes.storage: Keeps 3 days refrigerated and freezes well for 2 months. Reheat in a pan with 2-3 tbsp water over low heat; the fat will re-emulsify as it warms.

recipes.name: Lauki Kofta
recipes.subtitle: grated bottle gourd dumplings bound with besan, sitting in a plain onion-tomato gravy

ingredients.note: more only if the mix will not hold
keeps the koftas crisp

ingredients.qty: 500ml for frying, plus 3 tbsp for the gravy

ingredients.note: to finish

prepNotes: Grate the lauki and salt it for 20 minutes, then squeeze it dry over a bowl. Keep the squeezed juice — it goes into the gravy instead of plain water.
Mix the kofta batter only just before frying. Left standing, the lauki weeps again and the mix goes slack.
Fry the koftas and make the gravy separately, and combine them only 10 minutes before serving or they disintegrate.

steps.text: Squeeze the salted grated lauki hard, reserving the liquid. Mix the pulp with the besan, rice flour, half the grated ginger, the green chillies, 3 tbsp coriander leaves and salt into a mix that just holds a ball.
steps.tip: Add besan a tablespoon at a time. Too much and the koftas turn into hard besan balls.

steps.text: Heat the frying oil to 170C. Test with one kofta: it should sink, then rise in about 20 seconds without falling apart.
steps.tip: If the test kofta breaks up, work in another tablespoon of besan before frying the rest.

steps.text: Roll walnut-sized balls and fry 6-7 at a time for 4-5 minutes to a deep even brown. Drain on paper.
Blend the onion, garlic and remaining ginger to a coarse paste, and separately blend the tomatoes to a puree.
Heat 3 tbsp oil in a kadhai, crackle the cumin, then add the onion paste and fry 12 minutes on medium until it is golden and no longer smells raw.
Add the turmeric, kashmiri chilli, coriander and cumin powders and fry 1 minute with a splash of water.
Add the tomato puree and salt and cook 10-12 minutes until it thickens and the oil separates cleanly.
Lower the heat, beat in the whisked yogurt spoon by spoon, then cook 3 minutes.
steps.tip: The pan must be off a hard boil when the yogurt goes in, or it will curdle.

steps.text: Add the reserved lauki liquid made up to 400ml with hot water. Simmer 8 minutes until the gravy is smooth and coats a spoon.
Stir in the cream, crushed kasuri methi and garam masala. Slide the koftas in, cover and let them sit off the heat for 8 minutes to soak.
steps.tip: Do not boil the koftas in the gravy — they will fall apart. Off the heat is enough.

steps.text: Scatter the remaining coriander over and serve with roti or jeera rice.

recipes.storage: Store the koftas and gravy separately for up to 3 days refrigerated, combining only when reheating. Combined, they go mushy overnight. The gravy freezes 2 months; the koftas do not.

recipes.name: Mah Di Dal
recipes.subtitle: whole black urad simmered for hours with ginger and ghee, no cream and no tomato

ingredients.note: the traditional partner in a village mah di dal
use compounded-free hing to keep this gluten-free

prepNotes: Soak the whole urad and chana dal together overnight, at least 8 hours. This dal cannot be rushed with hot water.
This is the plain village dal, not dal makhani: no tomato, no cream, no butter finish. The creaminess comes only from the urad breaking down.
Keep 200ml of boiling water beside the pot for the long simmer.

steps.text: Drain the soaked dals and pressure cook with 1.2 litres water, the turmeric, half the crushed ginger, half the garlic and 1 tsp salt for 6 whistles, then 25 minutes on low.
Let the pressure drop naturally and open. The grains should be soft enough to crush against the side of the pot with a spoon.
steps.tip: If they still resist, cook another 10 minutes under pressure. Everything after this depends on the dal being fully soft.

steps.text: Mash about a third of the dal against the pot with the back of a ladle to thicken the liquid.
Simmer uncovered on the lowest heat for 35-40 minutes, stirring every 5 minutes and topping up with hot water when it gets too thick.
steps.tip: This slow open simmer is the whole recipe. Skipping it leaves you with boiled beans in water.

steps.text: In a small pan heat the ghee, add the cumin and asafoetida and let them foam for 15 seconds.
Add the onion and fry 8 minutes to a deep gold.
Add the remaining crushed garlic and the slit green chillies and fry 1 minute more.
Off the heat, stir in the chilli powder and coriander powder so they bloom in the residual heat without burning.
Pour the tadka into the dal, stir once, and simmer together 10 minutes.
Check the salt, add the garam masala and finish with the ginger matchsticks and coriander leaves. Serve with makki di roti or plain rice.

recipes.storage: Keeps 4 days refrigerated and is famously better the next day. It thickens hard when cold; reheat with 100ml hot water per portion, stirring until smooth. Freezes 2 months.

recipes.name: Makki di Roti
recipes.subtitle: coarse, crumbly winter flatbread patted out by hand and eaten hot with saag

ingredients.note: helps digestion and lifts the flavour

ingredients.qty: 3 tbsp, for the tawa and for serving

prepNotes: Boil the water and let it sit 2 minutes before using — hot water makes this glutenless dough far easier to handle.
Knead in small batches and keep the rest of the dough covered with a damp cloth; it dries out and cracks within minutes.
Cut two squares of baking paper or a clean plastic sheet to pat the rotis between — hand-patting takes practice.

steps.text: Mix the flour, salt and ajwain in a wide bowl.
Pour in the hot water a little at a time, mixing with a spoon at first, then knead 5 minutes with the heel of your hand into a smooth, pliable dough.
steps.tip: The dough should feel like soft clay. Too dry and it cracks; too wet and it sticks to everything.

steps.text: Cover and rest 10 minutes.
Divide into 8 balls. Roll one between your palms until it has no cracks on the surface.
Flatten it between two sheets of paper, pressing outward with your fingertips to a rough disc 5 inches across and about 5mm thick.
steps.tip: Thicker than a chapati, always. A thin makki roti falls apart when you lift it.

steps.text: Heat the tawa on medium until a drop of water skitters across it.
Peel the top sheet off, invert the roti onto your palm, and lay it on the tawa. Cook 90 seconds until the underside has pale brown freckles.
Flip and cook the second side 90 seconds, pressing the edges down with a cloth so it puffs slightly.
steps.tip: Press around the rim, not the middle, or you will squash the air out.

steps.text: Smear generously with ghee, flip once more for 20 seconds, and stack in a covered dish while you make the rest.
Serve immediately with butter melting on top and a bowl of saag.

recipes.storage: Best eaten straight off the tawa. They keep 4 hours wrapped in a cloth inside a covered box; revive on a hot tawa with a little ghee. They do not refrigerate well — the dough goes gritty.

recipes.name: Matar Paneer
recipes.subtitle: peas and paneer in a straightforward onion-tomato gravy, the weeknight standard

ingredients.note: or neutral oil
balances sharp tomatoes

prepNotes: If the paneer is firm from the fridge, soak the cubes in hot salted water 15 minutes and drain just before adding.
Blend the onion, tomato, ginger, garlic and chilli into a smooth paste and keep it ready — this gravy comes together fast.
Frozen peas go in at the end; fresh peas need 8 minutes of simmering.

steps.text: Blend the onion, tomato, ginger, garlic and green chillies to a smooth paste with 2 tbsp water.
Heat the ghee in a kadhai, add the bay leaf and cumin seeds, and let them crackle 20 seconds.
Pour in the blended paste — stand back, it spits — and cook on medium for 15 minutes.
steps.tip: Keep going until the paste darkens to brick red and oil clearly separates at the edges. Half-cooked paste tastes raw and metallic.

steps.text: Stir in the turmeric, coriander powder and kashmiri chilli and fry 1 minute.
Add 1.5 cups water, 1 tsp salt and the sugar, and bring to a simmer.
